content.latin: Veníte, exsultémus Dómino, iubilémus Deo, salutári nostro: præoccupémus fáciem eius in confessióne, et in psalmis iubilémus ei.
content.english: Come let us praise the Lord with joy: let us joyfully sing to God our saviour. Let us come before his presence with thanksgiving; and make a joyful noise to him with psalms.

content.latin: Quóniam Deus magnus Dóminus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos, quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: quia in manu eius sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitúdines móntium ipse cónspicit.
content.english: For the Lord is a great God, and a great King above all gods. For the Lord will not cast off his people: for in his hand are all the ends of the earth, and the heights of the mountains are his.

content.latin: Ant. Veníte adorémus.

content.latin: Quóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus eius (genuflectitur) veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos, quia ipse est Dóminus, Deus noster; nos autem pópulus eius, et oves páscuæ eius.
content.english: For the sea is his, and he made it: and his hands formed the dry land. (genuflect) Come let us adore and fall down: and weep before the Lord that made us: For he is the Lord our God: and we are the people of his pasture and the sheep of his hand.

content.latin: Hódie, si vocem eius audiéritis, nolíte obduráre corda vestra, sicut in exacerbatióne secúndum diem tentatiónis in desérto: ubi tentavérunt me patres vestri, probavérunt et vidérunt ópera mea.
content.english: Today if you shall hear his voice, harden not your hearts: As in the provocation, according to the day of temptation in the wilderness: where your fathers tempted me, they proved me, and saw my works.

content.latin: Quadragínta annis próximus fui generatióni huic, et dixi: Semper hi errant corde, ipsi vero non cognovérunt vias meas: quibus iurávi in ira mea: Si introíbunt in réquiem meam.
content.english: Forty years long was I offended with that generation, and I said: These always err in heart. And these men have not known my ways: so I swore in my wrath that they shall not enter into my rest.

content.latin: 5:2 Verba mea áuribus pércipe, Dómine, * intéllege clamórem meum.
content.english: 5:2 Give ear, O Lord, to my words * understand my cry.

segments.t: Verba mea áuribus pércipe, Dómine, * intéllege clamórem meum.

content.latin: 5:3 Inténde voci oratiónis meæ, * Rex meus et Deus meus.
content.english: 5:3 Hearken to the voice of my prayer, * O my King and my God.

segments.t: Inténde voci oratiónis meæ, * Rex meus et Deus meus.

content.latin: 5:4 Quóniam ad te orábo: * Dómine, mane exáudies vocem meam.
content.english: 5:4 For to thee will I pray: * O Lord, in the morning thou shalt hear my voice.

segments.t: Quóniam ad te orábo: * Dómine, mane exáudies vocem meam.

content.latin: 5:5 Mane astábo tibi et vidébo: * quóniam non Deus volens iniquitátem tu es.
content.english: 5:5 In the morning I will stand before thee, and will see: * because thou art not a God that willest iniquity.

segments.t: Mane astábo tibi et vidébo: * quóniam non Deus volens iniquitátem tu es.

content.latin: 5:6 Neque habitábit iuxta te malígnus: * neque permanébunt iniústi ante óculos tuos.
content.english: 5:6 Neither shall the wicked dwell near thee: * nor shall the unjust abide before thy eyes.

segments.t: Neque habitábit iuxta te malígnus: * neque permanébunt iniústi ante óculos tuos.

content.latin: 5:7 Odísti omnes, qui operántur iniquitátem: * perdes omnes, qui loquúntur mendácium.
content.english: 5:7 Thou hatest all the workers of iniquity: * thou wilt destroy all that speak a lie.

segments.t: Odísti omnes, qui operántur iniquitátem: * perdes omnes, qui loquúntur mendácium.

content.latin: 5:7 Virum sánguinum et dolósum abominábitur Dóminus: * ego autem in multitúdine misericórdiæ tuæ.
content.english: 5:7 The bloody and the deceitful man the Lord will abhor. * But as for me in the multitude of thy mercy,

segments.t: Virum sánguinum et dolósum abominábitur Dóminus: * ego autem in multitúdine misericórdiæ tuæ.

content.latin: 5:8 Introíbo in domum tuam: * adorábo ad templum sanctum tuum in timóre tuo.
content.english: 5:8 I will come into thy house; * I will worship towards thy holy temple, in thy fear.

segments.t: Introíbo in domum tuam: * adorábo ad templum sanctum tuum in timóre tuo.

content.latin: 5:9 Dómine, deduc me in iustítia tua: * propter inimícos meos dírige in conspéctu tuo viam meam.
content.english: 5:9 Conduct me, O Lord, in thy justice: * because of my enemies, direct my way in thy sight.

segments.t: Dómine, deduc me in iustítia tua: * propter inimícos meos dírige in conspéctu tuo viam meam.

content.latin: 5:10 Quóniam non est in ore eórum véritas: * cor eórum vanum est.
content.english: 5:10 For there is no truth in their mouth: * their heart is vain.

segments.t: Quóniam non est in ore eórum véritas: * cor eórum vanum est.

content.latin: 5:11 Sepúlcrum patens est guttur eórum, linguis suis dolóse agébant, * iúdica illos, Deus.
content.english: 5:11 Their throat is an open sepulchre: they dealt deceitfully with their tongues: * judge them, O God.

segments.t: Sepúlcrum patens est guttur eórum, linguis suis dolóse agébant, * iúdica illos, Deus.

content.latin: 5:11 Décidant a cogitatiónibus suis, secúndum multitúdinem impietátum eórum expélle eos, * quóniam irritavérunt te, Dómine.
content.english: 5:11 Let them fall from their devices: according to the multitude of their wickednesses cast them out: * for they have provoked thee, O Lord.

segments.t: Décidant a cogitatiónibus suis, secúndum multitúdinem impietátum eórum expélle eos, * quóniam irritavérunt te, Dómine.

content.latin: 5:12 Et læténtur omnes, qui sperant in te, * in ætérnum exsultábunt: et habitábis in eis.
content.english: 5:12 But let all them be glad that hope in thee: * they shall rejoice for ever, and thou shalt dwell in them.

segments.t: Et læténtur omnes, qui sperant in te, * in ætérnum exsultábunt: et habitábis in eis.

content.latin: 5:12 Et gloriabúntur in te omnes, qui díligunt nomen tuum, * quóniam tu benedíces iusto.
content.english: 5:12 And all they that love thy name shall glory in thee: * For thou wilt bless the just.

segments.t: Et gloriabúntur in te omnes, qui díligunt nomen tuum, * quóniam tu benedíces iusto.

content.latin: 5:13 Dómine, ut scuto bonæ voluntátis tuæ * coronásti nos.
content.english: 5:13 O Lord, thou hast crowned us, * as with a shield of thy good will.

segments.t: Dómine, ut scuto bonæ voluntátis tuæ * coronásti nos.

content.latin: 6:2 Dómine, ne in furóre tuo árguas me, * neque in ira tua corrípias me.
content.english: 6:2 Lord, rebuke me not in thy indignation, * nor chastise me in thy wrath.

segments.t: Dómine, ne in furóre tuo árguas me, * neque in ira tua corrípias me.

content.latin: 6:3 Miserére mei, Dómine, quóniam infírmus sum: * sana me, Dómine, quóniam conturbáta sunt ossa mea.
content.english: 6:3 Have mercy on me, O Lord, for I am weak: * heal me, O Lord, for my bones are troubled.

segments.t: Miserére mei, Dómine, quóniam infírmus sum: * sana me, Dómine, quóniam conturbáta sunt ossa mea.

content.latin: 6:4 Et ánima mea turbáta est valde: * sed tu, Dómine, úsquequo?
content.english: 6:4 And my soul is troubled exceedingly: * but thou, O Lord, how long?

segments.t: Et ánima mea turbáta est valde: * sed tu, Dómine, úsquequo?

content.latin: 6:5 Convértere, Dómine, et éripe ánimam meam: * salvum me fac propter misericórdiam tuam.
content.english: 6:5 Turn to me, O Lord, and deliver my soul: * O save me for thy mercy’s sake.

segments.t: Convértere, Dómine, et éripe ánimam meam: * salvum me fac propter misericórdiam tuam.

content.latin: 6:6 Quóniam non est in morte qui memor sit tui: * in inférno autem quis confitébitur tibi?
content.english: 6:6 For there is no one in death, that is mindful of thee: * and who shall confess to thee in hell?

segments.t: Quóniam non est in morte qui memor sit tui: * in inférno autem quis confitébitur tibi?

content.latin: 6:7 Laborávi in gémitu meo, lavábo per síngulas noctes lectum meum: * lácrimis meis stratum meum rigábo.
content.english: 6:7 I have laboured in my groanings, every night I will wash my bed: * I will water my couch with my tears.

segments.t: Laborávi in gémitu meo, lavábo per síngulas noctes lectum meum: * lácrimis meis stratum meum rigábo.

content.latin: 6:8 Turbátus est a furóre óculus meus: * inveterávi inter omnes inimícos meos.
content.english: 6:8 My eye is troubled through indignation: * I have grown old amongst all my enemies.

segments.t: Turbátus est a furóre óculus meus: * inveterávi inter omnes inimícos meos.

content.latin: 6:9 Discédite a me, omnes, qui operámini iniquitátem: * quóniam exaudívit Dóminus vocem fletus mei.
content.english: 6:9 Depart from me, all ye workers of iniquity: * for the Lord hath heard the voice of my weeping.

segments.t: Discédite a me, omnes, qui operámini iniquitátem: * quóniam exaudívit Dóminus vocem fletus mei.

content.latin: 6:10 Exaudívit Dóminus deprecatiónem meam, * Dóminus oratiónem meam suscépit.
content.english: 6:10 The Lord hath heard my supplication: * the Lord hath received my prayer.

segments.t: Exaudívit Dóminus deprecatiónem meam, * Dóminus oratiónem meam suscépit.

content.latin: 6:11 Erubéscant, et conturbéntur veheménter omnes inimíci mei: * convertántur et erubéscant valde velóciter.
content.english: 6:11 Let all my enemies be ashamed, and be very much troubled: * let them be turned back, and be ashamed very speedily.

segments.t: Erubéscant, et conturbéntur veheménter omnes inimíci mei: * convertántur et erubéscant valde velóciter.

content.english: Psalm 7 [3]

segments.t: Psalmus 7

content.latin: 7:2 Dómine, Deus meus, in te sperávi: * salvum me fac ex ómnibus persequéntibus me, et líbera me.
content.english: 7:2 O Lord my God, in thee have I put my trust: * save me from all them that persecute me, and deliver me.

segments.t: Dómine, Deus meus, in te sperávi: * salvum me fac ex ómnibus persequéntibus me, et líbera me.

content.latin: 7:3 Nequándo rápiat ut leo ánimam meam, * dum non est qui rédimat, neque qui salvum fáciat.
content.english: 7:3 Lest at any time he seize upon my soul like a lion, * while there is no one to redeem me, nor to save.

segments.t: Nequándo rápiat ut leo ánimam meam, * dum non est qui rédimat, neque qui salvum fáciat.

content.latin: 7:4 Dómine, Deus meus, si feci istud, * si est iníquitas in mánibus meis:
content.english: 7:4 O Lord my God, if I have done this thing, * if there be iniquity in my hands:

segments.t: Dómine, Deus meus, si feci istud, * si est iníquitas in mánibus meis:

content.latin: 7:5 Si réddidi retribuéntibus mihi mala, * décidam mérito ab inimícis meis inánis.
content.english: 7:5 If I have rendered to them that repaid me evils, * let me deservedly fall empty before my enemies.

segments.t: Si réddidi retribuéntibus mihi mala, * décidam mérito ab inimícis meis inánis.

content.latin: 7:6 Persequátur inimícus ánimam meam, et comprehéndat, et concúlcet in terra vitam meam, * et glóriam meam in púlverem dedúcat.
content.english: 7:6 Let the enemy pursue my soul, and take it, and tread down my life on the earth, * and bring down my glory to the dust.

segments.t: Persequátur inimícus ánimam meam, et comprehéndat, et concúlcet in terra vitam meam, * et glóriam meam in púlverem dedúcat.

content.latin: 7:7 Exsúrge, Dómine, in ira tua: * et exaltáre in fínibus inimicórum meórum.
content.english: 7:7 Rise up, O Lord, in thy anger: * and be thou exalted in the borders of my enemies.

segments.t: Exsúrge, Dómine, in ira tua: * et exaltáre in fínibus inimicórum meórum.

content.latin: 7:7 Et exsúrge, Dómine, Deus meus, in præcépto quod mandásti: * et synagóga populórum circúmdabit te.
content.english: 7:7 And arise, O Lord my God, in the precept which thou hast commanded: * and a congregation of people shall surround thee.

segments.t: Et exsúrge, Dómine, Deus meus, in præcépto quod mandásti: * et synagóga populórum circúmdabit te.

content.latin: 7:8 Et propter hanc in altum regrédere: * Dóminus iúdicat pópulos.
content.english: 7:8 And for their sakes return thou on high. * The Lord judgeth the people.

segments.t: Et propter hanc in altum regrédere: * Dóminus iúdicat pópulos.

content.latin: 7:9 Iúdica me, Dómine, secúndum iustítiam meam, * et secúndum innocéntiam meam super me.
content.english: 7:9 Judge me, O Lord, according to my justice, * and according to my innocence in me.

segments.t: Iúdica me, Dómine, secúndum iustítiam meam, * et secúndum innocéntiam meam super me.

content.latin: 7:10 Consumétur nequítia peccatórum, et díriges iustum, * scrutans corda et renes, Deus.
content.english: 7:10 The wickedness of sinners shall be brought to nought: and thou shalt direct the just: * the searcher of hearts and reins is God.

segments.t: Consumétur nequítia peccatórum, et díriges iustum, * scrutans corda et renes, Deus.

content.latin: 7:11 Iustum adiutórium meum a Dómino, * qui salvos facit rectos corde.
content.english: 7:11 Just is my help from the Lord: * who saveth the upright of heart.

segments.t: Iustum adiutórium meum a Dómino, * qui salvos facit rectos corde.

content.latin: 7:12 Deus iudex iustus, fortis, et pátiens: * numquid iráscitur per síngulos dies?
content.english: 7:12 God is a just judge, strong and patient: * is he angry every day?

segments.t: Deus iudex iustus, fortis, et pátiens: * numquid iráscitur per síngulos dies?

content.latin: 7:13 Nisi convérsi fuéritis, gládium suum vibrábit: * arcum suum teténdit, et parávit illum.
content.english: 7:13 Except you will be converted, he will brandish his sword: * he hath bent his bow, and made it ready.

segments.t: Nisi convérsi fuéritis, gládium suum vibrábit: * arcum suum teténdit, et parávit illum.

content.latin: 7:14 Et in eo parávit vasa mortis: * sagíttas suas ardéntibus effécit.
content.english: 7:14 And in it he hath prepared the instruments of death, * he hath made ready his arrows for them that burn.

segments.t: Et in eo parávit vasa mortis: * sagíttas suas ardéntibus effécit.

content.latin: 7:15 Ecce, partúriit iniustítiam: * concépit dolórem, et péperit iniquitátem.
content.english: 7:15 Behold he hath been in labour with injustice; * he hath conceived sorrow, and brought forth iniquity.

segments.t: Ecce, partúriit iniustítiam: * concépit dolórem, et péperit iniquitátem.

content.latin: 7:16 Lacum apéruit, et effódit eum: * et íncidit in fóveam quam fecit.
content.english: 7:16 He hath opened a pit and dug it: * and he is fallen into the hole he made.

segments.t: Lacum apéruit, et effódit eum: * et íncidit in fóveam quam fecit.

content.latin: 7:17 Convertétur dolor eius in caput eius: * et in vérticem ipsíus iníquitas eius descéndet.
content.english: 7:17 His sorrow shall be turned on his own head: * and his iniquity shall come down upon his crown.

segments.t: Convertétur dolor eius in caput eius: * et in vérticem ipsíus iníquitas eius descéndet.

content.latin: 7:18 Confitébor Dómino secúndum iustítiam eius: * et psallam nómini Dómini altíssimi.
content.english: 7:18 I will give glory to the Lord according to his justice: * and will sing to the name of the Lord the most High.

segments.t: Confitébor Dómino secúndum iustítiam eius: * et psallam nómini Dómini altíssimi.

segments.t: Pater Noster dicitur totum secreto.

content.latin: Pater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum: advéniat regnum tuum: fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum cotidiánum da nobis hódie: et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris: et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem: sed líbera nos a malo. Amen.
content.english: Our Father, who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us. And lead us not into temptation: But deliver us from evil. Amen.

content.latin: 16 Parce mihi, Dómine; nihil enim sunt dies mei.
content.english: 16 Spare me, for my days are nothing.

segments.t: Parce mihi, Dómine; nihil enim sunt dies mei.

content.latin: 17 Quid est homo, quia magníficas eum? aut quid appónis erga eum cor tuum?
content.english: 17 What is a man that thou shouldst magnify him? or why dost thou set thy heart upon him?

segments.t: Quid est homo, quia magníficas eum? aut quid appónis erga eum cor tuum?

content.latin: 18 Vísitas eum dilúculo, et súbito probas illum.
content.english: 18 Thou visitest him early in the morning, and thou provest him suddenly.

segments.t: Vísitas eum dilúculo, et súbito probas illum.

content.latin: 19 Usquequo non parcis mihi, nec dimíttis me, ut glútiam salívam meam?
content.english: 19 How long wilt thou not spare me, nor suffer me to swallow down my spittle?

segments.t: Usquequo non parcis mihi, nec dimíttis me, ut glútiam salívam meam?

content.latin: 20 Peccávi, quid fáciam tibi, o custos hóminum? quare posuísti me contrárium tibi, et factus sum mihimetípsi gravis?
content.english: 20 I have sinned: what shall I do to thee, O keeper of men? why hast thou set me opposite to thee, and I am become burdensome to myself?

segments.t: Peccávi, quid fáciam tibi, o custos hóminum? quare posuísti me contrárium tibi, et factus sum mihimetípsi gravis?

content.latin: 21 Cur non tollis peccátum meum, et quare non aufers iniquitátem meam? Ecce nunc in púlvere dórmiam: et, si mane me quæsíeris, non subsístam.
content.english: 21 Why dost thou not remove my sin, and why dost thou not take away my iniquity? Behold now I shall sleep in the dust: and if thou seek me in the morning, I shall not be.

segments.t: Cur non tollis peccátum meum, et quare non aufers iniquitátem meam? Ecce nunc in púlvere dórmiam: et, si mane me quæsíeris, non subsístam.

content.latin: ℟. Credo quod Redémptor meus vivit, et in novíssimo die de terra surrectúrus sum,
content.english: ℟. I believe that my Redeemer liveth, and that I shall stand up from the earth at the latter day,

segments.t: Credo quod Redémptor meus vivit, et in novíssimo die de terra surrectúrus sum,

content.latin: * Et in carne mea vidébo Deum Salvatórem meum.
content.english: * And in my flesh shall I see God my Saviour.

content.latin: ℣. Quem visúrus sum ego ipse, et non álius; et óculi mei conspectúri sunt.
content.english: ℣. Whom I shall see for myself, and mine eyes shall behold, and not another.

segments.t: Quem visúrus sum ego ipse, et non álius; et óculi mei conspectúri sunt.

content.latin: ℟. Et in carne mea vidébo Deum Salvatórem meum.
content.english: ℟. And in my flesh shall I see God my Saviour.

segments.t: Et in carne mea vidébo Deum Salvatórem meum.

content.latin: 1 Homo natus de mulíere, brevi vivens témpore, replétur multis misériis.
content.english: 1 Man born of a woman, living for a short time, is filled with many miseries.

segments.t: Homo natus de mulíere, brevi vivens témpore, replétur multis misériis.

content.latin: 2 Qui quasi flos egréditur et contéritur, et fugit velut umbra, et nunquam in eódem statu pérmanet.
content.english: 2 Who cometh forth like a flower, and is destroyed, and fleeth as a shadow, and never continueth in the same state.

segments.t: Qui quasi flos egréditur et contéritur, et fugit velut umbra, et nunquam in eódem statu pérmanet.

content.latin: 3 Et dignum ducis super huiuscémodi aperíre óculos tuos, et addúcere eum tecum in iudícium?
content.english: 3 And dost thou think it meet to open thy eyes upon such an one, and to bring him into judgment with thee?

segments.t: Et dignum ducis super huiuscémodi aperíre óculos tuos, et addúcere eum tecum in iudícium?

content.latin: 4 Quis potest fácere mundum de immúndo concéptum sémine? Nonne tu qui solus es?
content.english: 4 Who can make him clean that is conceived of unclean seed? is it not thou who only art?

segments.t: Quis potest fácere mundum de immúndo concéptum sémine? Nonne tu qui solus es?

content.latin: 5 Breves dies hóminis sunt: númerus ménsium eius apud te est: constituísti términos eius, qui præteríri non póterunt.
content.english: 5 The days of man are short, and the number of his months is with thee: thou hast appointed his bounds which cannot be passed.

segments.t: Breves dies hóminis sunt: númerus ménsium eius apud te est: constituísti términos eius, qui præteríri non póterunt.

content.latin: 6 Recéde páululum ab eo, ut quiéscat, donec optáta véniat, sicut mercenárii, dies eius.
content.english: 6 Depart a little from him, that he may rest, until his wished for day come, as that of the hireling

segments.t: Recéde páululum ab eo, ut quiéscat, donec optáta véniat, sicut mercenárii, dies eius.

content.latin: ℟. Qui Lázarum resuscitásti a monuménto fœ́tidum,
content.english: ℟. Thou Who didst call up Lazarus from the grave after that he had begun to stink

segments.t: Qui Lázarum resuscitásti a monuménto fœ́tidum,

content.latin: * Tu eis, Dómine, dona réquiem, et locum indulgéntiæ.
content.english: * Do Thou, O Lord, grant them rest and a place of forgiveness.

content.latin: ℣. Qui ventúrus es iudicáre vivos et mórtuos, et sǽculum per ignem.
content.english: ℣. Thou Who shalt come to judge the quick and dead, and the world by fire

segments.t: Qui ventúrus es iudicáre vivos et mórtuos, et sǽculum per ignem.

content.latin: ℟. Tu eis, Dómine, dona réquiem, et locum indulgéntiæ.
content.english: ℟. Do Thou, O Lord, grant them rest and a place of forgiveness.

segments.t: Tu eis, Dómine, dona réquiem, et locum indulgéntiæ.

content.latin: 20 Pelli meæ, consúmptis cárnibus, adhǽsit os meum, et derelícta sunt tantúmmodo lábia circa dentes meos.
content.english: 20 The flesh being consumed. My bone hath cleaved to my skin, and nothing but lips are left about my teeth.

segments.t: Pelli meæ, consúmptis cárnibus, adhǽsit os meum, et derelícta sunt tantúmmodo lábia circa dentes meos.

content.latin: 21 Miserémini mei, miserémini mei saltem vos, amíci mei, quia manus Dómini tétigit me.
content.english: 21 Have pity on me, have pity on me, at least you my friends, because the hand of the Lord hath touched me.

segments.t: Miserémini mei, miserémini mei saltem vos, amíci mei, quia manus Dómini tétigit me.

content.latin: 22 Quare persequímini me sicut Deus, et cárnibus meis saturámini?
content.english: 22 Why do you persecute me as God, and glut yourselves with my flesh?

segments.t: Quare persequímini me sicut Deus, et cárnibus meis saturámini?

content.latin: 23 Quis mihi tríbuat ut scribántur sermónes mei? quis mihi det ut exaréntur in libro
content.english: 23 Who will grant me that my words may be written? Who will grant me that they may be marked down in a book?

segments.t: Quis mihi tríbuat ut scribántur sermónes mei? quis mihi det ut exaréntur in libro

content.latin: 24 Stylo férreo et plumbi lámina, vel celte sculpántur in sílice?
content.english: 24 With an iron pen and in a plate of lead, or else be graven with an instrument in flint stone.

segments.t: Stylo férreo et plumbi lámina, vel celte sculpántur in sílice?

content.latin: 25 Scio enim quod redémptor meus vivit, et in novíssimo die de terra surrectúrus sum:
content.english: 25 For I know that my Redeemer liveth, and in the last day I shall rise out of the earth.

segments.t: Scio enim quod redémptor meus vivit, et in novíssimo die de terra surrectúrus sum:

content.latin: 26 Et rursum circúmdabor pelle mea, et in carne mea vidébo Deum meum:
content.english: 26 And I shall be clothed again with my skin, and in my flesh I will see my God.

segments.t: Et rursum circúmdabor pelle mea, et in carne mea vidébo Deum meum:

content.latin: 27 Quem visúrus sum ego ipse, et óculi mei conspectúri sunt, et non álius: repósita est hæc spes mea in sinu meo.
content.english: 27 Whom I myself shall see, and my eyes shall behold, and not another: this my hope is laid up in my bosom.

segments.t: Quem visúrus sum ego ipse, et óculi mei conspectúri sunt, et non álius: repósita est hæc spes mea in sinu meo.

content.latin: ℟. Dómine, quando véneris iudicáre terram, ubi me abscóndam a vultu iræ tuæ?
content.english: ℟. Lord, when Thou comest to judge the earth, where shall I hide myself from the face of thy wrath?

segments.t: Dómine, quando véneris iudicáre terram, ubi me abscóndam a vultu iræ tuæ?

content.latin: * Quia peccávi nimis in vita mea.
content.english: * For I have sinned greatly in my life.

content.latin: ℣. Commíssa mea pavésco, et ante te erubésco: dum véneris iudicáre, noli me condemnáre.
content.english: ℣. I dread my sins, I blush before thee I see the great tribunal set! In fear and terror I implore thee, Forgive when soul and Judge are met!

segments.t: Commíssa mea pavésco, et ante te erubésco: dum véneris iudicáre, noli me condemnáre.

content.latin: ℟. Quia peccávi nimis in vita mea.
content.english: ℟. For I have sinned greatly in my life.

segments.t: Quia peccávi nimis in vita mea.

content.latin: ℣. Réquiem ætérnam * dona eis, Dómine.
content.english: ℣. Eternal rest * grant unto them, O Lord.

segments.t: Réquiem ætérnam * dona eis, Dómine.

content.latin: ℟. Et lux perpétua * lúceat eis.
content.english: ℟. And let perpetual light * shine upon them.

segments.t: Et lux perpétua * lúceat eis.

content.latin: ℟. Quia peccávi nimis in vita mea.
content.english: ℟. For I have sinned greatly in my life.

segments.t: Quia peccávi nimis in vita mea.

content.latin: Nocturnus II
content.english: Nocturn II

segments.t: Nocturnus II

content.latin: Ant. In loco páscuæ * ibi me collocávit.
content.english: Ant. He maketh me to lie down * in green pastures.

segments.t: Ant.
In loco páscuæ * ibi me collocávit.

content.latin: Psalmus 22 [4]
content.english: Psalm 22 [4]

segments.t: Psalmus 22

content.latin: 22:1 Dóminus regit me, et nihil mihi déerit: * in loco páscuæ ibi me collocávit.
content.english: 22:1 The Lord ruleth me: and I shall want nothing. * He hath set me in a place of pasture.

segments.t: Dóminus regit me, et nihil mihi déerit: * in loco páscuæ ibi me collocávit.

content.latin: 22:2 Super aquam refectiónis educávit me: * ánimam meam convértit.
content.english: 22:2 He hath brought me up, on the water of refreshment: * he hath converted my soul.

segments.t: Super aquam refectiónis educávit me: * ánimam meam convértit.

content.latin: 22:3 Dedúxit me super sémitas iustítiæ, * propter nomen suum.
content.english: 22:3 He hath led me on the paths of justice, * for his own name’s sake.

segments.t: Dedúxit me super sémitas iustítiæ, * propter nomen suum.

content.latin: 22:4 Nam, et si ambulávero in médio umbræ mortis, non timébo mala: * quóniam tu mecum es.
content.english: 22:4 For though I should walk in the midst of the shadow of death, I will fear no evils, * for thou art with me.

segments.t: Nam, et si ambulávero in médio umbræ mortis, non timébo mala: * quóniam tu mecum es.

content.latin: 22:4 Virga tua, et báculus tuus: * ipsa me consoláta sunt.
content.english: 22:4 Thy rod and thy staff, * they have comforted me.

segments.t: Virga tua, et báculus tuus: * ipsa me consoláta sunt.

content.latin: 22:5 Parásti in conspéctu meo mensam, * advérsus eos, qui tríbulant me.
content.english: 22:5 Thou hast prepared a table before me * against them that afflict me.

segments.t: Parásti in conspéctu meo mensam, * advérsus eos, qui tríbulant me.

content.latin: 22:5 Impinguásti in óleo caput meum: * et calix meus inébrians quam præclárus est!
content.english: 22:5 Thou hast anointed my head with oil; * and my chalice which inebriateth me, how goodly is it!

segments.t: Impinguásti in óleo caput meum: * et calix meus inébrians quam præclárus est!

content.latin: 22:6 Et misericórdia tua subsequétur me * ómnibus diébus vitæ meæ:
content.english: 22:6 And thy mercy will follow me * all the days of my life.

segments.t: Et misericórdia tua subsequétur me * ómnibus diébus vitæ meæ:

content.latin: 22:6 Et ut inhábitem in domo Dómini, * in longitúdinem diérum.
content.english: 22:6 And that I may dwell in the house of the Lord * unto length of days.

segments.t: Et ut inhábitem in domo Dómini, * in longitúdinem diérum.

content.latin: ℣. Réquiem ætérnam * dona eis, Dómine.
content.english: ℣. Eternal rest * grant unto them, O Lord.

segments.t: Réquiem ætérnam * dona eis, Dómine.

content.latin: ℟. Et lux perpétua * lúceat eis.
content.english: ℟. And let perpetual light * shine upon them.

segments.t: Et lux perpétua * lúceat eis.

content.latin: Ant. In loco páscuæ ibi me collocávit.
content.english: Ant. He maketh me to lie down in green pastures.

segments.t: Ant.
In loco páscuæ ibi me collocávit.

content.latin: Ant. Delícta * iuventútis meæ, et ignorántias meas ne memíneris, Dómine.
content.english: Ant. Lord, remember not the sins of my youth, * nor my transgressions.

segments.t: Ant.
Delícta * iuventútis meæ, et ignorántias meas ne memíneris, Dómine.

content.latin: Psalmus 24 [5]
content.english: Psalm 24 [5]

segments.t: Psalmus 24

content.latin: 24:1 Ad te, Dómine, levávi ánimam meam: * Deus meus, in te confído, non erubéscam.
content.english: 24:1 To thee, O Lord, have I lifted up my soul: * In thee, O my God, I put my trust; let me not be ashamed.

segments.t: Ad te, Dómine, levávi ánimam meam: * Deus meus, in te confído, non erubéscam.

content.latin: 24:3 Neque irrídeant me inimíci mei: * étenim univérsi, qui sústinent te, non confundéntur.
content.english: 24:3 Neither let my enemies laugh at me: * for none of them that wait on thee shall be confounded.

segments.t: Neque irrídeant me inimíci mei: * étenim univérsi, qui sústinent te, non confundéntur.

content.latin: 24:4 Confundántur omnes iníqua agéntes * supervácue.
content.english: 24:4 Let all them be confounded that act unjust things * without cause.

segments.t: Confundántur omnes iníqua agéntes * supervácue.

content.latin: 24:4 Vias tuas, Dómine, demónstra mihi: * et sémitas tuas édoce me.
content.english: 24:4 Shew, O Lord, thy ways to me, * and teach me thy paths.

segments.t: Vias tuas, Dómine, demónstra mihi: * et sémitas tuas édoce me.

content.latin: 24:5 Dírige me in veritáte tua, et doce me: * quia tu es, Deus, salvátor meus, et te sustínui tota die.
content.english: 24:5 Direct me in thy truth, and teach me; * for thou art God my Saviour; and on thee have I waited all the day long.

segments.t: Dírige me in veritáte tua, et doce me: * quia tu es, Deus, salvátor meus, et te sustínui tota die.

content.latin: 24:6 Reminíscere miseratiónum tuárum, Dómine, * et misericordiárum tuárum, quæ a sǽculo sunt.
content.english: 24:6 Remember, O Lord, thy bowels of compassion; * and thy mercies that are from the beginning of the world.

segments.t: Reminíscere miseratiónum tuárum, Dómine, * et misericordiárum tuárum, quæ a sǽculo sunt.

content.latin: 24:7 Delícta iuventútis meæ, * et ignorántias meas ne memíneris.
content.english: 24:7 The sins of my youth * and my ignorances do not remember.

segments.t: Delícta iuventútis meæ, * et ignorántias meas ne memíneris.

content.latin: 24:7 Secúndum misericórdiam tuam meménto mei tu: * propter bonitátem tuam, Dómine.
content.english: 24:7 According to thy mercy remember thou me: * for thy goodness’ sake, O Lord.

segments.t: Secúndum misericórdiam tuam meménto mei tu: * propter bonitátem tuam, Dómine.

content.latin: 24:8 Dulcis et rectus Dóminus: * propter hoc legem dabit delinquéntibus in via.
content.english: 24:8 The Lord is sweet and righteous: * therefore he will give a law to sinners in the way.

segments.t: Dulcis et rectus Dóminus: * propter hoc legem dabit delinquéntibus in via.

content.latin: 24:9 Díriget mansuétos in iudício: * docébit mites vias suas.
content.english: 24:9 He will guide the mild in judgment: * he will teach the meek his ways.

segments.t: Díriget mansuétos in iudício: * docébit mites vias suas.

content.latin: 24:10 Univérsæ viæ Dómini, misericórdia et véritas, * requiréntibus testaméntum eius et testimónia eius.
content.english: 24:10 All the ways of the Lord are mercy and truth, * to them that seek after his covenant and his testimonies.

segments.t: Univérsæ viæ Dómini, misericórdia et véritas, * requiréntibus testaméntum eius et testimónia eius.

content.latin: 24:11 Propter nomen tuum, Dómine, propitiáberis peccáto meo: * multum est enim.
content.english: 24:11 For thy name’s sake, O Lord, thou wilt pardon my sin: * for it is great.

segments.t: Propter nomen tuum, Dómine, propitiáberis peccáto meo: * multum est enim.

content.latin: 24:12 Quis est homo qui timet Dóminum? * legem státuit ei in via, quam elégit.
content.english: 24:12 Who is the man that feareth the Lord? * He hath appointed him a law in the way he hath chosen.

segments.t: Quis est homo qui timet Dóminum? * legem státuit ei in via, quam elégit.

content.latin: 24:13 Ánima eius in bonis demorábitur: * et semen eius hereditábit terram.
content.english: 24:13 His soul shall dwell in good things: * and his seed shall inherit the land.

segments.t: Ánima eius in bonis demorábitur: * et semen eius hereditábit terram.

content.latin: 24:14 Firmaméntum est Dóminus timéntibus eum: * et testaméntum ipsíus ut manifestétur illis.
content.english: 24:14 The Lord is a firmament to them that fear him: * and his covenant shall be made manifest to them.

segments.t: Firmaméntum est Dóminus timéntibus eum: * et testaméntum ipsíus ut manifestétur illis.

content.latin: 24:15 Óculi mei semper ad Dóminum: * quóniam ipse evéllet de láqueo pedes meos.
content.english: 24:15 My eyes are ever towards the Lord: * for he shall pluck my feet out of the snare.

segments.t: Óculi mei semper ad Dóminum: * quóniam ipse evéllet de láqueo pedes meos.

content.latin: 24:16 Réspice in me, et miserére mei: * quia únicus et pauper sum ego.
content.english: 24:16 Look thou upon me, and have mercy on me; * for I am alone and poor.

segments.t: Réspice in me, et miserére mei: * quia únicus et pauper sum ego.

content.latin: 24:17 Tribulatiónes cordis mei multiplicátæ sunt: * de necessitátibus meis érue me.
content.english: 24:17 The troubles of my heart are multiplied: * deliver me from my necessities.

segments.t: Tribulatiónes cordis mei multiplicátæ sunt: * de necessitátibus meis érue me.

content.latin: 24:18 Vide humilitátem meam, et labórem meum: * et dimítte univérsa delícta mea.
content.english: 24:18 See my abjection and my labour; * and forgive me all my sins.

segments.t: Vide humilitátem meam, et labórem meum: * et dimítte univérsa delícta mea.

content.latin: 24:19 Réspice inimícos meos quóniam multiplicáti sunt, * et ódio iníquo odérunt me.
content.english: 24:19 Consider my enemies for they are multiplied, * and have hated me with an unjust hatred.

segments.t: Réspice inimícos meos quóniam multiplicáti sunt, * et ódio iníquo odérunt me.

content.latin: 24:20 Custódi ánimam meam, et érue me: * non erubéscam quóniam sperávi in te.
content.english: 24:20 Keep thou my soul, and deliver me: * I shall not be ashamed, for I have hoped in thee.

segments.t: Custódi ánimam meam, et érue me: * non erubéscam quóniam sperávi in te.

content.latin: 24:21 Innocéntes et recti adhæsérunt mihi: * quia sustínui te.
content.english: 24:21 The innocent and the upright have adhered to me: * because I have waited on thee.

segments.t: Innocéntes et recti adhæsérunt mihi: * quia sustínui te.

content.latin: 24:22 Líbera, Deus, Israël, * ex ómnibus tribulatiónibus suis.
content.english: 24:22 Deliver Israel, O God, * from all his tribulations.

segments.t: Líbera, Deus, Israël, * ex ómnibus tribulatiónibus suis.

content.latin: ℣. Réquiem ætérnam * dona eis, Dómine.
content.english: ℣. Eternal rest * grant unto them, O Lord.

segments.t: Réquiem ætérnam * dona eis, Dómine.

content.latin: ℟. Et lux perpétua * lúceat eis.
content.english: ℟. And let perpetual light * shine upon them.

segments.t: Et lux perpétua * lúceat eis.

content.latin: Ant. Delícta iuventútis meæ, et ignorántias meas ne memíneris, Dómine.
content.english: Ant. Lord, remember not the sins of my youth, nor my transgressions.

segments.t: Ant.
Delícta iuventútis meæ, et ignorántias meas ne memíneris, Dómine.

content.latin: Ant. Credo vidére * bona Dómini in terra vivéntium.
content.english: Ant. I believe that I shall yet see the goodness of the Lord * in the land of the living.

segments.t: Ant.
Credo vidére * bona Dómini in terra vivéntium.

content.latin: Psalmus 26 [6]
content.english: Psalm 26 [6]

segments.t: Psalmus 26

content.latin: 26:1 Dóminus illuminátio mea, et salus mea, * quem timébo?
content.english: 26:1 The Lord is my light and my salvation, * whom shall I fear?

segments.t: Dóminus illuminátio mea, et salus mea, * quem timébo?

content.latin: 26:1 Dóminus protéctor vitæ meæ, * a quo trepidábo?
content.english: 26:1 The Lord is the protector of my life: * of whom shall I be afraid?

content.latin: Pater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum: advéniat regnum tuum: fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum cotidiánum da nobis hódie: et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris: et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem: sed líbera nos a malo. Amen.
content.english: Our Father, who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us. And lead us not into temptation: But deliver us from evil. Amen.

content.latin: Ex Libro sancti Augustíni Epíscopi de cura pro mórtuis gerénda
content.english: From the book of St. Augustine, the Bishop, on the Care for the Deceased

content.latin: Cap 2 et 3
content.english: Cap. 2 & 3

segments.t: Cap 2 et 3

content.latin: Curátio fúneris, condítio sepultúræ, pompa exsequiárum magis sunt vivórum solácia quam subsídia mortuórum. Nec ídeo tamen contemnénda et abiciénda sunt córpora defunctórum, maximéque iustórum ac fidélium, quibus tamquam órganis et vasis ad ómnia bona ópera sancte usus est spíritus. Si enim patérna vestis et ánulus, ac si quid huiúsmodi, tanto cárius est pósteris, quanto erga paréntes maior afféctus; nullo modo ipsa spernénda sunt córpora, quæ útique multo familiárius atque coniúnctius quam quǽlibet induménta gestámus. Hæc enim non ad ornaméntum vel adiutórium, quod adhibétur extrínsecus, sed ad ipsam natúram hóminis pértinent. Unde et antiquórum iustórum fúnera officiósa pietáte curáta sunt, et exséquiæ celebrátæ, et sepultúra provísa; ipsíque, cum víverent, de sepeliéndis vel étiam transferéndis suis corpóribus fíliis mandavérunt.
content.english: If this be true, doubtless also the providing for the interment of bodies a place at the Memorials of Saints, is a mark of a good human affection towards the remains of one's friends. Yet it follows not that the bodies of the departed are to be despised and flung aside, and above all of just and faithful men, which bodies as organs and vessels to all good works their spirit has holily used. For if a father's garment and ring, and whatever such like, is the more dear to those whom they leave behind, the greater their affection is towards their parents, in no wise are the bodies themselves to be spurned, which truly we wear in more familiar and close conjunction than any of our putting on. For these pertain not to ornament or aid which is applied from without, but to the very nature of man. Whence also the funerals of the just men of old were with dutiful piety cared for, and their obsequies celebrated, and sepulture provided: and themselves while living did touching burial or even translation of their bodies give charge to their sons.

content.latin: Cap. 4

content.latin: Recordántis et precántis afféctus cum defúnctis a fidélibus caríssimis exhibétur, eum prodésse non dúbium est iis, qui cum in córpore víverent, tália sibi post hanc vitam prodésse meruérunt. Verum, etsi áliqua necéssitas vel humári córpora, vel in sacris locis humári nulla data facultáte permíttat, non sunt prætermitténdæ supplicatiónes pro spirítibus mortuórum: quas faciéndas pro ómnibus in christiána et cathólica societáte defúnctis, étiam tácitis eórum nomínibus, sub generáli commemoratióne suscépit Ecclésia; ut quibus ad ista desunt paréntes, aut fílii, aut quicúmque cognáti vel amíci, ab una eis exhibeántur pia matre commúni. Si autem deéssent istæ supplicatiónes, quæ fiunt recta fide ac pietáte pro mórtuis, puto quod nihil prodésset spirítibus eórum, quámlibet in locis sanctis exánima córpora poneréntur.
content.english: And when this affection is exhibited to the departed by faithful men who were most dear to them, there is no doubt that it profits them who while living in the body merited that such things should profit them after this life. But even if some necessity should through absence of all facility not allow bodies to be interred, or in such places interred, yet should there be no pretermitting of supplications for the spirits of the dead: which supplications, that they should be made for all in Christian and catholic fellowship departed, even without mentioning of their names, under a general commemoration, the Church has charged herself withal; to the intent that they which lack, for these offices, parents or sons or whatever kindred or friends, may have the same afforded unto them by the one pious mother which is common to all. But if there were lack of these supplications, which are made with right faith and piety for the dead, I account that it should not a whit profit their spirits, howsoever in holy places the lifeless bodies should be deposited.

content.latin: Quæ cum ita sint, non existimémus ad mórtuos, pro quibus curam gérimus, perveníre, nisi quod pro eis sive altáris, sive oratiónum, sive eleemosynárum sacrifíciis solémniter supplicámus: quamvis non pro quibus fiunt, ómnibus prosint; sed iis tantum pro quibus, dum vivunt, comparátur, ut prosint. Sed quia non discérnimus qui sunt, opórtet ea pro regenerátis ómnibus fácere, ut nullus eórum prætermittátur, ad quos hæc benefícia possint et débeant perveníre. Mélius enim supérerunt ista eis, quibus nec obsunt nec prosunt; quam eis déerunt, quibus prosunt. Diligéntius tamen facit hæc quisque pro necessáriis suis, quo pro illo fiat simíliter a suis. Córpori autem humándo quidquid impénditur, non est præsídium salútis, sed humanitátis offícium, secúndum afféctum quo nemo unquam carnem suam ódio habet. Unde opórtet ut quam potest pro carne próximi curam gerat, cum ille inde recésserit, qui gerébat. Et si hæc fáciunt, qui carnis resurrectiónem non credunt, quanto magis debent fácere qui credunt; ut córpori mórtuo, sed tamen resurrectúro et in æternitáte mansúro, impénsum eiúsmodi offícium sit étiam quodámmodo eiúsdem fídei testimónium!
content.english: Which things being so, let us not think that to the dead for whom we have a care, any thing reaches save what by sacrifices either of the altar, or of prayers, or of alms, we solemnly supplicate: although not to all for whom they are done be they profitable, but to them only by whom while they live it is obtained that they should be profitable. But forasmuch as we discern not who these be, it is meet to do them for all regenerate persons, that none of them may be passed by to whom these benefits may and ought to reach. For better it is that these things shall be superfluously done to them whom they neither hinder nor help, than lacking to them whom they help. More diligently however does each man these things for his own near and dear friends, in order that they may be likewise done unto him by his. But as for the burying of the body, whatever is bestowed on that, is no aid of salvation, but an office of humanity, according to that affection by which no man ever hates his own flesh. Whence it is fitting that he take what care he is able for the flesh of his neighbor, when he is gone that bare it. And if they do these things who believe not the resurrection of the flesh, how much more are they beholden to do the same who do believe; that so, an office of this kind bestowed upon a body, dead but yet to rise again and to remain to eternity, may also be in some sort a testimony of the same faith?

segments.t: Multiplicátæ sunt super capíllos cápitis mei: * et cor meum derelíquit me.

content.latin: 39:14 Compláceat tibi, Dómine, ut éruas me: * Dómine, ad adiuvándum me réspice.
content.english: 39:14 Be pleased, O Lord to deliver me: * look down, O Lord, to help me.

segments.t: Compláceat tibi, Dómine, ut éruas me: * Dómine, ad adiuvándum me réspice.

content.latin: 39:15 Confundántur et revereántur simul, qui quærunt ánimam meam, * ut áuferant eam.
content.english: 39:15 Let them be confounded and ashamed together, that seek after my soul * to take it away.

segments.t: Confundántur et revereántur simul, qui quærunt ánimam meam, * ut áuferant eam.

content.latin: 39:15 Convertántur retrórsum, et revereántur, * qui volunt mihi mala.
content.english: 39:15 Let them be turned backward and be ashamed * that desire evils to me.

segments.t: Convertántur retrórsum, et revereántur, * qui volunt mihi mala.

content.latin: 39:16 Ferant conféstim confusiónem suam, * qui dicunt mihi: Euge, euge.
content.english: 39:16 Let them immediately bear their confusion, * that say to me: ’T is well, ’t is well.

segments.t: Ferant conféstim confusiónem suam, * qui dicunt mihi: Euge, euge.

content.latin: 39:17 Exsúltent et læténtur super te omnes quæréntes te: * et dicant semper: Magnificétur Dóminus: qui díligunt salutáre tuum.
content.english: 39:17 Let all that seek thee rejoice and be glad in thee: * and let such as love thy salvation say always: The Lord be magnified.

segments.t: Exsúltent et læténtur super te omnes quæréntes te: * et dicant semper: Magnificétur Dóminus: qui díligunt salutáre tuum.

content.latin: 39:18 Ego autem mendícus sum, et pauper: * Dóminus sollícitus est mei.
content.english: 39:18 But I am a beggar and poor: * the Lord is careful for me.

segments.t: Ego autem mendícus sum, et pauper: * Dóminus sollícitus est mei.

content.latin: 39:18 Adiútor meus, et protéctor meus tu es: * Deus meus, ne tardáveris.
content.english: 39:18 Thou art my helper and my protector: * O my God, be not slack.

segments.t: Adiútor meus, et protéctor meus tu es: * Deus meus, ne tardáveris.

content.latin: ℣. Réquiem ætérnam * dona eis, Dómine.
content.english: ℣. Eternal rest * grant unto them, O Lord.

segments.t: Réquiem ætérnam * dona eis, Dómine.

content.latin: ℟. Et lux perpétua * lúceat eis.
content.english: ℟. And let perpetual light * shine upon them.

segments.t: Et lux perpétua * lúceat eis.

content.latin: Ant. Compláceat tibi, Dómine, ut erípias me: Dómine, ad adiuvándum me réspice.
content.english: Ant. Be pleased, O Lord, to deliver me O Lord, look upon me to help me.

segments.t: Ant.
Compláceat tibi, Dómine, ut erípias me: Dómine, ad adiuvándum me réspice.

content.latin: Ant. Sana, Dómine, * ánimam meam, quia peccávi tibi.
content.english: Ant. Lord, heal my soul; * for I have sinned against thee.

segments.t: Ant.
Sana, Dómine, * ánimam meam, quia peccávi tibi.

content.latin: Psalmus 40 [8]
content.english: Psalm 40 [8]

segments.t: Psalmus 40

content.latin: 40:2 Beátus qui intéllegit super egénum, et páuperem: * in die mala liberábit eum Dóminus.
content.english: 40:2 Blessed is he that understandeth concerning the needy and the poor: * the Lord will deliver him in the evil day.

segments.t: Beátus qui intéllegit super egénum, et páuperem: * in die mala liberábit eum Dóminus.

content.latin: 40:3 Dóminus consérvet eum, et vivíficet eum, et beátum fáciat eum in terra: * et non tradat eum in ánimam inimicórum eius.
content.english: 40:3 The Lord preserve him and give him life, and make him blessed upon the earth: * and deliver him not up to the will of his enemies.

segments.t: Dóminus consérvet eum, et vivíficet eum, et beátum fáciat eum in terra: * et non tradat eum in ánimam inimicórum eius.

content.latin: 40:4 Dóminus opem ferat illi super lectum dolóris eius: * univérsum stratum eius versásti in infirmitáte eius.
content.english: 40:4 The Lord help him on his bed of sorrow: * thou hast turned all his couch in his sickness.

segments.t: Dóminus opem ferat illi super lectum dolóris eius: * univérsum stratum eius versásti in infirmitáte eius.

content.latin: 40:5 Ego dixi: Dómine, miserére mei: * sana ánimam meam, quia peccávi tibi.
content.english: 40:5 I said: O Lord, be thou merciful to me: * heal my soul, for I have sinned against thee.

segments.t: Ego dixi: Dómine, miserére mei: * sana ánimam meam, quia peccávi tibi.

content.latin: 40:6 Inimíci mei dixérunt mala mihi: * Quando moriétur, et períbit nomen eius?
content.english: 40:6 My enemies have spoken evils against me: * when shall he die and his name perish?

segments.t: Inimíci mei dixérunt mala mihi: * Quando moriétur, et períbit nomen eius?

content.latin: 40:7 Et si ingrediebátur ut vidéret, vana loquebátur: * cor eius congregávit iniquitátem sibi.
content.english: 40:7 And if he came in to see me, he spoke vain things: * his heart gathered together iniquity to itself.

segments.t: Et si ingrediebátur ut vidéret, vana loquebátur: * cor eius congregávit iniquitátem sibi.

content.latin: 40:7 Egrediebátur foras, * et loquebátur in idípsum.
content.english: 40:7 He went out * and spoke to the same purpose.

segments.t: Egrediebátur foras, * et loquebátur in idípsum.

content.latin: 40:8 Advérsum me susurrábant omnes inimíci mei: * advérsum me cogitábant mala mihi.
content.english: 40:8 All my enemies whispered together against me: * they devised evils to me.

segments.t: Advérsum me susurrábant omnes inimíci mei: * advérsum me cogitábant mala mihi.

content.latin: 40:9 Verbum iníquum constituérunt advérsum me: * Numquid qui dormit non adíciet ut resúrgat?
content.english: 40:9 They determined against me an unjust word: * shall he that sleepeth rise again no more?

segments.t: Verbum iníquum constituérunt advérsum me: * Numquid qui dormit non adíciet ut resúrgat?

content.latin: 40:10 Étenim homo pacis meæ, in quo sperávi: * qui edébat panes meos, magnificávit super me supplantatiónem.
content.english: 40:10 For even the man of my peace, in whom I trusted, * who ate my bread, hath greatly supplanted me.

segments.t: Étenim homo pacis meæ, in quo sperávi: * qui edébat panes meos, magnificávit super me supplantatiónem.

content.latin: 40:11 Tu autem, Dómine, miserére mei, et resúscita me: * et retríbuam eis.
content.english: 40:11 But thou, O Lord, have mercy on me, and raise me up again: * and I will requite them.

segments.t: Tu autem, Dómine, miserére mei, et resúscita me: * et retríbuam eis.

content.latin: 40:12 In hoc cognóvi quóniam voluísti me: * quóniam non gaudébit inimícus meus super me.
content.english: 40:12 By this I know, that thou hast had a good will for me: * because my enemy shall not rejoice over me.

segments.t: In hoc cognóvi quóniam voluísti me: * quóniam non gaudébit inimícus meus super me.

content.latin: 40:13 Me autem propter innocéntiam suscepísti: * et confirmásti me in conspéctu tuo in ætérnum.
content.english: 40:13 But thou hast upheld me by reason of my innocence: * and hast established me in thy sight for ever.

segments.t: Me autem propter innocéntiam suscepísti: * et confirmásti me in conspéctu tuo in ætérnum.

content.latin: 40:14 Benedíctus Dóminus, Deus Israël, a sǽculo et usque in sǽculum: * fiat, fiat.
content.english: 40:14 Blessed be the Lord the God of Israel from eternity to eternity. * So be it. So be it.

segments.t: Benedíctus Dóminus, Deus Israël, a sǽculo et usque in sǽculum: * fiat, fiat.

content.latin: ℣. Réquiem ætérnam * dona eis, Dómine.
content.english: ℣. Eternal rest * grant unto them, O Lord.

segments.t: Réquiem ætérnam * dona eis, Dómine.

content.latin: ℟. Et lux perpétua * lúceat eis.
content.english: ℟. And let perpetual light * shine upon them.

segments.t: Et lux perpétua * lúceat eis.

content.latin: Ant. Sana, Dómine, ánimam meam, quia peccávi tibi.
content.english: Ant. Lord, heal my soul; for I have sinned against thee.

segments.t: Ant.
Sana, Dómine, ánimam meam, quia peccávi tibi.

content.latin: Ant. Sitívit * ánima mea ad Deum vivum: quando véniam, et apparébo ante fáciem Dómini?
content.english: Ant. My soul thirsteth for the living God; * when shall I come and appear before God?

segments.t: Ant.
Sitívit * ánima mea ad Deum vivum: quando véniam, et apparébo ante fáciem Dómini?

content.latin: Psalmus 41 [9]
content.english: Psalm 41 [9]

segments.t: Psalmus 41

content.latin: 41:2 Quemádmodum desíderat cervus ad fontes aquárum: * ita desíderat ánima mea ad te, Deus.
content.english: 41:2 As the hart panteth after the fountains of water; * so my soul panteth after thee, O God.

segments.t: Quemádmodum desíderat cervus ad fontes aquárum: * ita desíderat ánima mea ad te, Deus.

content.latin: 41:3 Sitívit ánima mea ad Deum fortem vivum: * quando véniam, et apparébo ante fáciem Dei?
content.english: 41:3 My soul hath thirsted after the strong living God; * when shall I come and appear before the face of God?

segments.t: Sitívit ánima mea ad Deum fortem vivum: * quando véniam, et apparébo ante fáciem Dei?

content.latin: 41:4 Fuérunt mihi lácrimæ meæ panes die ac nocte: * dum dícitur mihi cotídie: Ubi est Deus tuus?
content.english: 41:4 My tears have been my bread day and night, * whilst it is said to me daily: Where is thy God?

segments.t: Fuérunt mihi lácrimæ meæ panes die ac nocte: * dum dícitur mihi cotídie: Ubi est Deus tuus?

content.latin: 41:5 Hæc recordátus sum, et effúdi in me ánimam meam: * quóniam transíbo in locum tabernáculi admirábilis, usque ad domum Dei.
content.english: 41:5 These things I remembered, and poured out my soul in me: * for I shall go over into the place of the wonderful tabernacle, even to the house of God:

segments.t: Hæc recordátus sum, et effúdi in me ánimam meam: * quóniam transíbo in locum tabernáculi admirábilis, usque ad domum Dei.

content.latin: 41:5 In voce exsultatiónis, et confessiónis: * sonus epulántis.
content.english: 41:5 With the voice of joy and praise; * the noise of one feasting.

segments.t: In voce exsultatiónis, et confessiónis: * sonus epulántis.

content.latin: 41:6 Quare tristis es, ánima mea? * et quare contúrbas me?
content.english: 41:6 Why art thou sad, O my soul? * and why dost thou trouble me?

segments.t: Quare tristis es, ánima mea? * et quare contúrbas me?

content.latin: 41:6 Spera in Deo, quóniam adhuc confitébor illi: * salutáre vultus mei, et Deus meus.
content.english: 41:6 Hope in God, for I will still give praise to him: * the salvation of my countenance, and my God.

segments.t: Spera in Deo, quóniam adhuc confitébor illi: * salutáre vultus mei, et Deus meus.

content.latin: 41:7 Ad meípsum ánima mea conturbáta est: * proptérea memor ero tui de terra Iordánis, et Hermóniim a monte módico.
content.english: 41:7 My soul is troubled within myself: * therefore will I remember thee from the land of Jordan and Hermoniim, from the little hill.

segments.t: Ad meípsum ánima mea conturbáta est: * proptérea memor ero tui de terra Iordánis, et Hermóniim a monte módico.

content.latin: 41:8 Abýssus abýssum ínvocat, * in voce cataractárum tuárum.
content.english: 41:8 Deep calleth on deep, * at the noise of thy flood-gates.

segments.t: Abýssus abýssum ínvocat, * in voce cataractárum tuárum.

content.latin: 41:8 Ómnia excélsa tua, et fluctus tui * super me transiérunt.
content.english: 41:8 All thy heights and thy billows * have passed over me.

segments.t: Ómnia excélsa tua, et fluctus tui * super me transiérunt.

content.latin: 41:9 In die mandávit Dóminus misericórdiam suam: * et nocte cánticum eius.
content.english: 41:9 In the daytime the Lord hath commanded his mercy; * and a canticle to him in the night.

segments.t: In die mandávit Dóminus misericórdiam suam: * et nocte cánticum eius.

content.latin: 41:9 Apud me orátio Deo vitæ meæ, * dicam Deo: Suscéptor meus es.
content.english: 41:9 With me is prayer to the God of my life. * I will say to God: Thou art my support.

segments.t: Apud me orátio Deo vitæ meæ, * dicam Deo: Suscéptor meus es.

content.latin: 41:10 Quare oblítus es mei? * et quare contristátus incédo, dum afflígit me inimícus?
content.english: 41:10 Why hast thou forgotten me? * and why go I mourning, whilst my enemy afflicteth me?

segments.t: Quare oblítus es mei? * et quare contristátus incédo, dum afflígit me inimícus?

content.latin: 41:11 Dum confringúntur ossa mea, * exprobravérunt mihi qui tríbulant me inimíci mei.
content.english: 41:11 Whilst my bones are broken, * my enemies who trouble me have reproached me;

segments.t: Dum confringúntur ossa mea, * exprobravérunt mihi qui tríbulant me inimíci mei.

content.latin: 41:11 Dum dicunt mihi per síngulos dies: Ubi est Deus tuus? * quare tristis es, ánima mea? et quare contúrbas me?
content.english: 41:11 Whilst they say to me day by day: Where is thy God? * Why art thou cast down, O my soul? and why dost thou disquiet me?

segments.t: Dum dicunt mihi per síngulos dies: Ubi est Deus tuus? * quare tristis es, ánima mea? et quare contúrbas me?

content.latin: 41:12 Spera in Deo, quóniam adhuc confitébor illi: * salutáre vultus mei, et Deus meus.
content.english: 41:12 Hope thou in God, for I will still give praise to him: * the salvation of my countenance, and my God.

segments.t: Spera in Deo, quóniam adhuc confitébor illi: * salutáre vultus mei, et Deus meus.

content.latin: ℣. Réquiem ætérnam * dona eis, Dómine.
content.english: ℣. Eternal rest * grant unto them, O Lord.

segments.t: Réquiem ætérnam * dona eis, Dómine.

content.latin: ℟. Et lux perpétua * lúceat eis.
content.english: ℟. And let perpetual light * shine upon them.

segments.t: Et lux perpétua * lúceat eis.

content.latin: Ant. Sitívit ánima mea ad Deum vivum: quando véniam, et apparébo ante fáciem Dómini?
content.english: Ant. My soul thirsteth for the living God; when shall I come and appear before God?

segments.t: Ant.
Sitívit ánima mea ad Deum vivum: quando véniam, et apparébo ante fáciem Dómini?

content.latin: ℣. Ne tradas béstiis ánimas confiténtes tibi.
content.english: ℣. O deliver not unto beasts the souls of them that praise thee!

segments.t: Ne tradas béstiis ánimas confiténtes tibi.

content.latin: ℟. Et ánimas páuperum tuórum ne obliviscáris in finem.
content.english: ℟. And forget not the souls of thy poor for ever.

segments.t: Et ánimas páuperum tuórum ne obliviscáris in finem.

content.latin: Pater Noster dicitur totum secreto.
content.english: Our Father is said completely in silence.

segments.t: Pater Noster dicitur totum secreto.

content.latin: Pater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum: advéniat regnum tuum: fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum cotidiánum da nobis hódie: et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris: et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem: sed líbera nos a malo. Amen.
content.english: Our Father, who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us. And lead us not into temptation: But deliver us from evil. Amen.

content.latin: De Epístola prima beáti Pauli Apóstoli ad Corínthios
content.english: From the first letter of St. Paul to the Corinthians

content.latin: 12 Si Christus prædicátur quod resurréxit a mórtuis, quómodo quidam dicunt in vobis, quóniam resurréctio mortuórum non est?
content.english: 12 Now if Christ be preached, that he arose again from the dead, how do some among you say, that there is no resurrection of the dead?

segments.t: Si Christus prædicátur quod resurréxit a mórtuis, quómodo quidam dicunt in vobis, quóniam resurréctio mortuórum non est?

content.latin: 13 Si autem resurréctio mortuórum non est: neque Christus resurréxit.
content.english: 13 But if there be no resurrection of the dead, then Christ is not risen again.

segments.t: Si autem resurréctio mortuórum non est: neque Christus resurréxit.

content.latin: 14 Si autem Christus non resurréxit, inánis est ergo prædicátio nostra, inánis est et fides vestra:
content.english: 14 And if Christ be not risen again, then is our preaching vain, and your faith is also vain.

segments.t: Si autem Christus non resurréxit, inánis est ergo prædicátio nostra, inánis est et fides vestra:

content.latin: 15 Invenímur autem et falsi testes Dei: quóniam testimónium díximus advérsus Deum quod suscitáverit Christum, quem non suscitávit, si mórtui non resúrgunt.
content.english: 15 Yea, and we are found false witnesses of God: because we have given testimony against God, that he hath raised up Christ; whom he hath not raised up, if the dead rise not again.

segments.t: Invenímur autem et falsi testes Dei: quóniam testimónium díximus advérsus Deum quod suscitáverit Christum, quem non suscitávit, si mórtui non resúrgunt.

content.latin: 16 Nam si mórtui non resúrgunt, neque Christus resurréxit.
content.english: 16 For if the dead rise not again, neither is Christ risen again.

segments.t: Nam si mórtui non resúrgunt, neque Christus resurréxit.

content.latin: 17 Quod si Christus non resurréxit, vana est fides vestra: adhuc enim estis in peccátis vestris.
content.english: 17 And if Christ be not risen again, your faith is vain, for you are yet in your sins.

segments.t: Quod si Christus non resurréxit, vana est fides vestra: adhuc enim estis in peccátis vestris.

content.latin: 18 Ergo et qui dormiérunt in Christo, periérunt.
content.english: 18 Then they also that are fallen asleep in Christ, are perished.

segments.t: Ergo et qui dormiérunt in Christo, periérunt.

content.latin: 19 Si in hac vita tantum in Christo sperántes sumus, miserabilióres sumus ómnibus homínibus.
content.english: 19 If in this life only we have hope in Christ, we are of all men most miserable.

segments.t: Si in hac vita tantum in Christo sperántes sumus, miserabilióres sumus ómnibus homínibus.

content.latin: 20 Nunc autem Christus resurréxit a mórtuis primítiæ dormiéntium,
content.english: 20 But now Christ is risen from the dead, the firstfruits of them that sleep

segments.t: Nunc autem Christus resurréxit a mórtuis primítiæ dormiéntium,

content.latin: 21 Quóniam quidem per hóminem mors, et per hóminem resurréctio mortuórum.
content.english: 21 For by a man came death, and by a man the resurrection of the dead.

segments.t: Quóniam quidem per hóminem mors, et per hóminem resurréctio mortuórum.

content.latin: 22 Et sicut in Adam omnes moriúntur, ita et in Christo omnes vivificabúntur.
content.english: 22 And as in Adam all die, so also in Christ all shall be made alive.

segments.t: Et sicut in Adam omnes moriúntur, ita et in Christo omnes vivificabúntur.

content.latin: ℟. Peccántem me cotídie, et non me pœniténtem, timor mortis contúrbat me:
content.english: ℟. Forasmuch as I sin daily, and repent not, the fear of death troubleth me.

segments.t: Peccántem me cotídie, et non me pœniténtem, timor mortis contúrbat me:

content.latin: * Quia in inférno nulla est redémptio, miserére mei, Deus, et salva me.
content.english: * O God, have mercy upon me, and save me, for in hell there is no redemption.

content.latin: ℣. Deus, in nómine tuo salvum me fac, et in virtúte tua líbera me.
content.english: ℣. Save me, O God, by thy name, and judge me in thy strength.

segments.t: Deus, in nómine tuo salvum me fac, et in virtúte tua líbera me.

content.latin: ℟. Quia in inférno nulla est redémptio, miserére mei, Deus, et salva me.
content.english: ℟. O God, have mercy upon me, and save me, for in hell there is no redemption.

segments.t: Quia in inférno nulla est redémptio, miserére mei, Deus, et salva me.

content.latin: 35 Sed dicet áliquis: Quómodo resúrgunt mórtui? qualíve córpore vénient?
content.english: 35 But some man will say: How do the dead rise again? or with what manner of body shall they come?

segments.t: Sed dicet áliquis: Quómodo resúrgunt mórtui? qualíve córpore vénient?

content.latin: 36 Insípiens, tu quod séminas non vivificátur, nisi prius moriátur:
content.english: 36 Senseless man, that which thou sowest is not quickened, except it die first.

segments.t: Insípiens, tu quod séminas non vivificátur, nisi prius moriátur:

content.latin: 37 Et quod séminas, non corpus, quod futúrum est, séminas, sed nudum granum, ut puta trítici, aut alicúius ceterórum.
content.english: 37 And that which thou sowest, thou sowest not the body that shall be; but bare grain, as of wheat, or of some of the rest.

segments.t: Et quod séminas, non corpus, quod futúrum est, séminas, sed nudum granum, ut puta trítici, aut alicúius ceterórum.

content.latin: 38 Deus autem dat illi corpus sicut vult, et unicuíque séminum próprium corpus.
content.english: 38 But God giveth it a body as he will: and to every seed its proper body.

segments.t: Deus autem dat illi corpus sicut vult, et unicuíque séminum próprium corpus.

content.latin: 39 Non omnis caro, éadem caro: sed ália quidem hóminum, ália vero pécorum, ália vólucrum, ália autem píscium.
content.english: 39 All flesh is not the same flesh: but one is the flesh of men, another of beasts, another of birds, another of fishes.

segments.t: Non omnis caro, éadem caro: sed ália quidem hóminum, ália vero pécorum, ália vólucrum, ália autem píscium.

content.latin: 40 Et córpora cæléstia, et córpora terréstria: sed ália quidem cæléstium glória, ália autem terréstrium.
content.english: 40 And there are bodies celestial, and bodies terrestrial: but, one is the glory of the celestial, and another of the terrestrial.

segments.t: Et córpora cæléstia, et córpora terréstria: sed ália quidem cæléstium glória, ália autem terréstrium.

content.latin: 41 Alia cláritas solis, ália cláritas lunæ, et ália cláritas stellárum; stella enim a stella differt in claritáte:
content.english: 41 One is the glory of the sun, another the glory of the moon, and another the glory of the stars. For star differeth from star in glory.

segments.t: Alia cláritas solis, ália cláritas lunæ, et ália cláritas stellárum; stella enim a stella differt in claritáte:

content.latin: 42 Sic et resurréctio mortuórum. Seminátur in corruptióne, surget in incorruptióne.
content.english: 42 So also is the resurrection of the dead. It is sown in corruption, it shall rise in incorruption.

segments.t: Sic et resurréctio mortuórum. Seminátur in corruptióne, surget in incorruptióne.

content.latin: 43 Seminátur in ignobilitáte, surget in glória: seminátur in infirmitáte, surget in virtúte:
content.english: 43 It is sown in dishonour, it shall rise in glory. It is sown in weakness, it shall rise in power.

segments.t: Seminátur in ignobilitáte, surget in glória: seminátur in infirmitáte, surget in virtúte:

content.latin: 44 Seminátur corpus animále, surget corpus spiritále.
content.english: 44 It is sown a natural body, it shall rise a spiritual body.

segments.t: Seminátur corpus animále, surget corpus spiritále.

content.latin: ℟. Dómine, secúndum actum meum noli me iudicáre: nihil dignum in conspéctu tuo egi; ídeo déprecor maiestátem tuam,
content.english: ℟. O Lord, judge me not according to my works; for I have done nothing that can be counted in respect of thee. I beseech thy majesty therefore, that thou wouldest

segments.t: Dómine, secúndum actum meum noli me iudicáre: nihil dignum in conspéctu tuo egi; ídeo déprecor maiestátem tuam,

content.latin: * Ut tu, Deus, déleas iniquitátem meam.
content.english: * Blot out my transgressions, O God.

content.latin: ℣. Amplius lava me, Dómine, ab iniustítia mea, et a delícto meo munda me.
content.english: ℣. Lord, wash me thoroughly from mine iniquity and cleanse me from my sin.

segments.t: Amplius lava me, Dómine, ab iniustítia mea, et a delícto meo munda me.

content.latin: ℟. Ut tu, Deus, déleas iniquitátem meam.
content.english: ℟. Blot out my transgressions, O God.

segments.t: Ut tu, Deus, déleas iniquitátem meam.

content.latin: 51 Ecce mystérium vobis dico: Omnes quidem resurgémus, sed non omnes immutábimur.
content.english: 51 Behold, I tell you a mystery. We shall all indeed rise again: but we shall not all be changed.

segments.t: Ecce mystérium vobis dico: Omnes quidem resurgémus, sed non omnes immutábimur.

content.latin: 52 In moménto, in ictu óculi, in novíssima tuba: canet enim tuba, et mórtui resúrgent incorrúpti: et nos immutábimur.
content.english: 52 In a moment, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trumpet: for the trumpet shall sound, and the dead shall rise again incorruptible: and we shall be changed.

segments.t: In moménto, in ictu óculi, in novíssima tuba: canet enim tuba, et mórtui resúrgent incorrúpti: et nos immutábimur.

content.latin: 53 Opórtet enim corruptíbile hoc indúere incorruptiónem: et mortále hoc indúere immortalitátem.
content.english: 53 For this corruptible must put on incorruption; and this mortal must put on immortality.

segments.t: Opórtet enim corruptíbile hoc indúere incorruptiónem: et mortále hoc indúere immortalitátem.

content.latin: 54 Cum autem mortále hoc indúerit immortalitátem, tunc fiet sermo, qui scriptus est: Absórpta est mors in victória.
content.english: 54 And when this mortal hath put on immortality, then shall come to pass the saying that is written: Death is swallowed up in victory.

segments.t: Cum autem mortále hoc indúerit immortalitátem, tunc fiet sermo, qui scriptus est: Absórpta est mors in victória.

content.latin: 55 Ubi est mors victória tua? ubi est mors stímulus tuus?
content.english: 55 O death, where is thy victory? O death, where is thy sting?

segments.t: Ubi est mors victória tua? ubi est mors stímulus tuus?

content.latin: 56 Stímulus autem mortis peccátum est: virtus vero peccáti lex.
content.english: 56 Now the sting of death is sin: and the power of sin is the law.

segments.t: Stímulus autem mortis peccátum est: virtus vero peccáti lex.

content.latin: 57 Deo autem grátias, qui dedit nobis victóriam per Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum.
content.english: 57 But thanks be to God, who hath given us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ.

segments.t: Deo autem grátias, qui dedit nobis victóriam per Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum.

content.latin: 58 Itaque fratres mei dilécti, stábiles estóte, et immóbiles: abundántes in ópere Dómini semper, sciéntes quod labor vester non est inánis in Dómino.
content.english: 58 Therefore, my beloved brethren, be ye steadfast and unmoveable; always abounding in the work of the Lord, knowing that your labour is not in vain in the Lord.

segments.t: Itaque fratres mei dilécti, stábiles estóte, et immóbiles: abundántes in ópere Dómini semper, sciéntes quod labor vester non est inánis in Dómino.

content.latin: ℟. Líbera me, Dómine, de morte ætérna in die illa treménda,
content.english: ℟. Deliver me, O Lord, from eternal death in that awful day

segments.t: Líbera me, Dómine, de morte ætérna in die illa treménda,

content.english: * when the heavens and the earth shall be shaken, and Thou shalt come to judge the world by fire.

content.english: ℣. Quaking and dread take hold upon me, when I look for the coming of the trial and the wrath to come.

segments.t: Tremens factus sum ego et tímeo, dum discússio vénerit atque ventúra ira.

content.latin: ℟. Quando cæli movéndi sunt et terra.
content.english: ℟. When the heavens and the earth shall be shaken.

segments.t: Quando cæli movéndi sunt et terra.

content.latin: ℣. Dies illa, dies iræ, calamitátis et misériæ, dies magna et amára valde.
content.english: ℣. That day is a day of wrath, of wasteness and desolation, a great day and exceeding bitter.

segments.t: Dies illa, dies iræ, calamitátis et misériæ, dies magna et amára valde.

content.latin: ℟. Dum véneris iudicáre sǽculum per ignem.
content.english: ℟. When Thou shalt come to judge the world by fire.

segments.t: Dum véneris iudicáre sǽculum per ignem.

content.english: ℣. Eternal rest * grant unto them, O Lord.

segments.t: Réquiem ætérnam * dona eis, Dómine.

content.english: ℟. And let perpetual light * shine upon them.

content.latin: Reliqua omittuntur, nisi separandæ sint.
content.english: Skip the rest, unless praying separately.

segments.t: Reliqua omittuntur, nisi separandæ sint.

content.latin: ℣. Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.
content.english: ℣. O Lord, hear my prayer.

segments.t: Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.

content.latin: ℟. Et clamor meus ad te véniat.
content.english: ℟. And let my cry come unto thee.

segments.t: Et clamor meus ad te véniat.

content.latin: Orémus.
content.english: Let us pray.

content.latin: Fidélium, Deus, ómnium Cónditor et Redémptor, animábus famulórum famularúmque tuárum remissiónem cunctórum tríbue peccatórum: ut indulgéntiam, quam semper optavérunt, piis supplicatiónibus consequántur:
content.english: O God, who art thyself at once the Maker and the Redeemer of all thy faithful ones, grant unto the souls of thy servants and handmaids remission of all their sins, making of our entreaties unto our great Father a mean whereby they may have that forgiveness which they have ever hoped for.

content.latin: Qui vivis et regnas cum Deo Patre, in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: Who livest and reignest with God the Father in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, world without end.

content.latin: Psalmus 50 [1]
content.english: Psalm 50 [1]

segments.t: Psalmus 50

content.latin: 50:3 Miserére mei, Deus, * secúndum magnam misericórdiam tuam.
content.english: 50:3 Have mercy on me, O God, * according to thy great mercy.

segments.t: Miserére mei, Deus, * secúndum magnam misericórdiam tuam.

content.latin: 50:3 Et secúndum multitúdinem miseratiónum tuárum, * dele iniquitátem meam.
content.english: 50:3 And according to the multitude of thy tender mercies * blot out my iniquity.

segments.t: Et secúndum multitúdinem miseratiónum tuárum, * dele iniquitátem meam.

content.latin: 50:4 Ámplius lava me ab iniquitáte mea: * et a peccáto meo munda me.
content.english: 50:4 Wash me yet more from my iniquity, * and cleanse me from my sin.

segments.t: Ámplius lava me ab iniquitáte mea: * et a peccáto meo munda me.

content.latin: 50:5 Quóniam iniquitátem meam ego cognósco: * et peccátum meum contra me est semper.
content.english: 50:5 For I know my iniquity, * and my sin is always before me.

segments.t: Quóniam iniquitátem meam ego cognósco: * et peccátum meum contra me est semper.

content.latin: 50:6 Tibi soli peccávi, et malum coram te feci: * ut iustificéris in sermónibus tuis, et vincas cum iudicáris.
content.english: 50:6 To thee only have I sinned, and have done evil before thee: * that thou mayst be justified in thy words, and mayst overcome when thou art judged.

segments.t: Tibi soli peccávi, et malum coram te feci: * ut iustificéris in sermónibus tuis, et vincas cum iudicáris.

content.latin: 50:7 Ecce enim, in iniquitátibus concéptus sum: * et in peccátis concépit me mater mea.
content.english: 50:7 For behold I was conceived in iniquities; * and in sins did my mother conceive me.

segments.t: Ecce enim, in iniquitátibus concéptus sum: * et in peccátis concépit me mater mea.

content.latin: 50:8 Ecce enim, veritátem dilexísti: * incérta et occúlta sapiéntiæ tuæ manifestásti mihi.
content.english: 50:8 For behold thou hast loved truth: * the uncertain and hidden things of thy wisdom thou hast made manifest to me.

segments.t: Ecce enim, veritátem dilexísti: * incérta et occúlta sapiéntiæ tuæ manifestásti mihi.

content.latin: 50:9 Aspérges me hyssópo, et mundábor: * lavábis me, et super nivem dealbábor.
content.english: 50:9 Thou shalt sprinkle me with hyssop, and I shall be cleansed: * thou shalt wash me, and I shall be made whiter than snow.

segments.t: Aspérges me hyssópo, et mundábor: * lavábis me, et super nivem dealbábor.

content.latin: 50:10 Audítui meo dabis gáudium et lætítiam: * et exsultábunt ossa humiliáta.
content.english: 50:10 To my hearing thou shalt give joy and gladness: * and the bones that have been humbled shall rejoice.

segments.t: Audítui meo dabis gáudium et lætítiam: * et exsultábunt ossa humiliáta.

content.latin: 50:11 Avérte fáciem tuam a peccátis meis: * et omnes iniquitátes meas dele.
content.english: 50:11 Turn away thy face from my sins, * and blot out all my iniquities.

segments.t: Avérte fáciem tuam a peccátis meis: * et omnes iniquitátes meas dele.

content.latin: 50:12 Cor mundum crea in me, Deus: * et spíritum rectum ínnova in viscéribus meis.
content.english: 50:12 Create a clean heart in me, O God: * and renew a right spirit within my bowels.

segments.t: Cor mundum crea in me, Deus: * et spíritum rectum ínnova in viscéribus meis.

content.latin: 50:13 Ne proícias me a fácie tua: * et spíritum sanctum tuum ne áuferas a me.
content.english: 50:13 Cast me not away from thy face; * and take not thy holy spirit from me.

segments.t: Ne proícias me a fácie tua: * et spíritum sanctum tuum ne áuferas a me.

content.latin: 50:14 Redde mihi lætítiam salutáris tui: * et spíritu principáli confírma me.
content.english: 50:14 Restore unto me the joy of thy salvation, * and strengthen me with a perfect spirit.

segments.t: Redde mihi lætítiam salutáris tui: * et spíritu principáli confírma me.

content.latin: 50:15 Docébo iníquos vias tuas: * et ímpii ad te converténtur.
content.english: 50:15 I will teach the unjust thy ways: * and the wicked shall be converted to thee.

segments.t: Docébo iníquos vias tuas: * et ímpii ad te converténtur.

content.latin: 50:16 Líbera me de sanguínibus, Deus, Deus salútis meæ: * et exsultábit lingua mea iustítiam tuam.
content.english: 50:16 Deliver me from blood, O God, thou God of my salvation: * and my tongue shall extol thy justice.

segments.t: Líbera me de sanguínibus, Deus, Deus salútis meæ: * et exsultábit lingua mea iustítiam tuam.

content.latin: 50:17 Dómine, lábia mea apéries: * et os meum annuntiábit laudem tuam.
content.english: 50:17 O Lord, thou wilt open my lips: * and my mouth shall declare thy praise.

segments.t: Dómine, lábia mea apéries: * et os meum annuntiábit laudem tuam.

content.latin: 50:18 Quóniam si voluísses sacrifícium, dedíssem útique: * holocáustis non delectáberis.
content.english: 50:18 For if thou hadst desired sacrifice, I would indeed have given it: * with burnt offerings thou wilt not be delighted.

segments.t: Quóniam si voluísses sacrifícium, dedíssem útique: * holocáustis non delectáberis.

content.latin: 50:19 Sacrifícium Deo spíritus contribulátus: * cor contrítum, et humiliátum, Deus, non despícies.
content.english: 50:19 A sacrifice to God is an afflicted spirit: * a contrite and humbled heart, O God, thou wilt not despise.

segments.t: Sacrifícium Deo spíritus contribulátus: * cor contrítum, et humiliátum, Deus, non despícies.

content.latin: 50:20 Benígne fac, Dómine, in bona voluntáte tua Sion: * ut ædificéntur muri Ierúsalem.
content.english: 50:20 Deal favourably, O Lord, in thy good will with Sion; * that the walls of Jerusalem may be built up.

segments.t: Benígne fac, Dómine, in bona voluntáte tua Sion: * ut ædificéntur muri Ierúsalem.

content.latin: 50:21 Tunc acceptábis sacrifícium iustítiæ, oblatiónes, et holocáusta: * tunc impónent super altáre tuum vítulos.
content.english: 50:21 Then shalt thou accept the sacrifice of justice, oblations and whole burnt offerings: * then shall they lay calves upon thy altar.

segments.t: Tunc acceptábis sacrifícium iustítiæ, oblatiónes, et holocáusta: * tunc impónent super altáre tuum vítulos.

content.latin: ℣. Réquiem ætérnam * dona eis, Dómine.
content.english: ℣. Eternal rest * grant unto them, O Lord.

segments.t: Réquiem ætérnam * dona eis, Dómine.

content.latin: ℟. Et lux perpétua * lúceat eis.
content.english: ℟. And let perpetual light * shine upon them.

segments.t: Et lux perpétua * lúceat eis.
