content.english: Psalm 64 [2]

segments.t: Psalmus 64

content.latin: 64:2 Te decet hymnus, Deus, in Sion: * et tibi reddétur votum in Ierúsalem.
content.english: 64:2 A hymn, O God, becometh thee in Sion: * and a vow shall be paid to thee in Jerusalem.

segments.t: Te decet hymnus, Deus, in Sion: * et tibi reddétur votum in Ierúsalem.

content.latin: 64:3 Exáudi oratiónem meam: * ad te omnis caro véniet.
content.english: 64:3 O hear my prayer: * all flesh shall come to thee.

segments.t: Exáudi oratiónem meam: * ad te omnis caro véniet.

content.latin: 64:4 Verba iniquórum prævaluérunt super nos: * et impietátibus nostris tu propitiáberis.
content.english: 64:4 The words of the wicked have prevailed over us: * and thou wilt pardon our transgressions.

segments.t: Verba iniquórum prævaluérunt super nos: * et impietátibus nostris tu propitiáberis.

content.latin: 64:5 Beátus, quem elegísti, et assumpsísti: * inhabitábit in átriis tuis.
content.english: 64:5 Blessed is he whom thou hast chosen and taken to thee: * he shall dwell in thy courts.

segments.t: Beátus, quem elegísti, et assumpsísti: * inhabitábit in átriis tuis.

content.latin: 64:5 Replébimur in bonis domus tuæ: * sanctum est templum tuum, mirábile in æquitáte.
content.english: 64:5 We shall be filled with the good things of thy house; holy is thy temple, * wonderful in justice.

segments.t: Replébimur in bonis domus tuæ: * sanctum est templum tuum, mirábile in æquitáte.

content.latin: 64:6 Exáudi nos, Deus, salutáris noster, * spes ómnium fínium terræ, et in mari longe.
content.english: 64:6 Hear us, O God our saviour, * who art the hope of all the ends of the earth, and in the sea afar off.

segments.t: Exáudi nos, Deus, salutáris noster, * spes ómnium fínium terræ, et in mari longe.

content.latin: 64:7 Prǽparans montes in virtúte tua, accínctus poténtia: * qui contúrbas profúndum maris sonum flúctuum eius.
content.english: 64:7 Thou who preparest the mountains by thy strength, being girded with power: * who troublest the depth of the sea, the noise of its waves.

segments.t: Prǽparans montes in virtúte tua, accínctus poténtia: * qui contúrbas profúndum maris sonum flúctuum eius.

content.latin: 64:8 Turbabúntur gentes, et timébunt qui hábitant términos a signis tuis: * éxitus matutíni, et véspere delectábis.
content.english: 64:8 The Gentiles shall be troubled, and they that dwell in the uttermost borders shall be afraid at thy signs: * thou shalt make the outgoings of the morning and of the evening to be joyful.

segments.t: Turbabúntur gentes, et timébunt qui hábitant términos a signis tuis: * éxitus matutíni, et véspere delectábis.

content.latin: 64:10 Visitásti terram, et inebriásti eam: * multiplicásti locupletáre eam.
content.english: 64:10 Thou hast visited the earth, and hast plentifully watered it; * thou hast many ways enriched it.

segments.t: Visitásti terram, et inebriásti eam: * multiplicásti locupletáre eam.

content.latin: 64:10 Flumen Dei replétum est aquis, parásti cibum illórum: * quóniam ita est præparátio eius.
content.english: 64:10 The river of God is filled with water, thou hast prepared their food; * for so is its preparation.

segments.t: Flumen Dei replétum est aquis, parásti cibum illórum: * quóniam ita est præparátio eius.

content.latin: 64:11 Rivos eius inébria, multíplica genímina eius: * in stillicídiis eius lætábitur gérminans.
content.english: 64:11 Fill up plentifully the streams thereof, multiply its fruits; * it shall spring up and rejoice in its showers.

segments.t: Rivos eius inébria, multíplica genímina eius: * in stillicídiis eius lætábitur gérminans.

content.latin: 64:12 Benedíces corónæ anni benignitátis tuæ: * et campi tui replebúntur ubertáte.
content.english: 64:12 Thou shalt bless the crown of the year of thy goodness: * and thy fields shall be filled with plenty.

segments.t: Benedíces corónæ anni benignitátis tuæ: * et campi tui replebúntur ubertáte.

content.latin: 64:13 Pinguéscent speciósa desérti: * et exsultatióne colles accingéntur.
content.english: 64:13 The beautiful places of the wilderness shall grow fat: * and the hills shall be girded about with joy.

segments.t: Pinguéscent speciósa desérti: * et exsultatióne colles accingéntur.

content.latin: 64:14 Indúti sunt aríetes óvium, et valles abundábunt fruménto: * clamábunt, étenim hymnum dicent.
content.english: 64:14 The rams of the flock are clothed, and the vales shall abound with corn: * they shall shout, yea they shall sing a hymn.

segments.t: Indúti sunt aríetes óvium, et valles abundábunt fruménto: * clamábunt, étenim hymnum dicent.

segments.t: Réquiem ætérnam * dona eis, Dómine.

content.english: Ant. Thy right hand * upholdeth me.

Me suscépit * déxtera tua, Dómine.

content.english: Psalm 62 [3]

segments.t: Psalmus 62

content.latin: 62:2 Deus, Deus meus, * ad te de luce vígilo.
content.english: 62:2 O God, my God, * to thee do I watch at break of day.

segments.t: Deus, Deus meus, * ad te de luce vígilo.

content.latin: 62:2 Sitívit in te ánima mea, * quam multiplíciter tibi caro mea.
content.english: 62:2 For thee my soul hath thirsted; * for thee my flesh, O how many ways!

segments.t: Sitívit in te ánima mea, * quam multiplíciter tibi caro mea.

content.latin: 62:3 In terra desérta, et ínvia, et inaquósa: * sic in sancto appárui tibi, ut vidérem virtútem tuam, et glóriam tuam.
content.english: 62:3 In a desert land, and where there is no way, and no water: * so in the sanctuary have I come before thee, to see thy power and thy glory.

segments.t: In terra desérta, et ínvia, et inaquósa: * sic in sancto appárui tibi, ut vidérem virtútem tuam, et glóriam tuam.

content.latin: 62:4 Quóniam mélior est misericórdia tua super vitas: * lábia mea laudábunt te.
content.english: 62:4 For thy mercy is better than lives: * thee my lips shall praise.

segments.t: Quóniam mélior est misericórdia tua super vitas: * lábia mea laudábunt te.

content.latin: 62:5 Sic benedícam te in vita mea: * et in nómine tuo levábo manus meas.
content.english: 62:5 Thus will I bless thee all my life long: * and in thy name I will lift up my hands.

segments.t: Sic benedícam te in vita mea: * et in nómine tuo levábo manus meas.

content.latin: 62:6 Sicut ádipe et pinguédine repleátur ánima mea: * et lábiis exsultatiónis laudábit os meum.
content.english: 62:6 Let my soul be filled as with marrow and fatness: * and my mouth shall praise thee with joyful lips.

segments.t: Sicut ádipe et pinguédine repleátur ánima mea: * et lábiis exsultatiónis laudábit os meum.

content.latin: 62:7 Si memor fui tui super stratum meum, in matutínis meditábor in te: * quia fuísti adiútor meus.
content.english: 62:7 If I have remembered thee upon my bed, I will meditate on thee in the morning: * because thou hast been my helper.

segments.t: Si memor fui tui super stratum meum, in matutínis meditábor in te: * quia fuísti adiútor meus.

content.latin: 62:8 Et in velaménto alárum tuárum exsultábo, adhǽsit ánima mea post te: * me suscépit déxtera tua.
content.english: 62:8 And I will rejoice under the covert of thy wings: my soul hath stuck close to thee: * thy right hand hath received me.

segments.t: Et in velaménto alárum tuárum exsultábo, adhǽsit ánima mea post te: * me suscépit déxtera tua.

content.latin: 62:10 Ipsi vero in vanum quæsiérunt ánimam meam, introíbunt in inferióra terræ: * tradéntur in manus gládii, partes vúlpium erunt.
content.english: 62:10 But they have sought my soul in vain, they shall go into the lower parts of the earth: * they shall be delivered into the hands of the sword, they shall be the portions of foxes.

segments.t: Ipsi vero in vanum quæsiérunt ánimam meam, introíbunt in inferióra terræ: * tradéntur in manus gládii, partes vúlpium erunt.

content.latin: 62:12 Rex vero lætábitur in Deo, laudabúntur omnes qui iurant in eo: * quia obstrúctum est os loquéntium iníqua.
content.english: 62:12 But the king shall rejoice in God, all they shall be praised that swear by him: * because the mouth is stopped of them that speak wicked things.

segments.t: Rex vero lætábitur in Deo, laudabúntur omnes qui iurant in eo: * quia obstrúctum est os loquéntium iníqua.

content.english: Canticle of Ezechias [4]

segments.t: Canticum Ezechiæ

content.latin: 38:10 Ego dixi: In dimídio diérum meórum * vadam ad portas ínferi.
content.english: 38:10 I said: In the midst of my days * I shall go to the gates of hell:

segments.t: Ego dixi: In dimídio diérum meórum * vadam ad portas ínferi.

content.latin: 38:11 Quæsívi resíduum annórum meórum. * Dixi: Non vidébo Dóminum Deum in terra vivéntium.
content.english: 38:11 I sought for the residue of my years. * I said: I shall not see the Lord God in the land of the living.

segments.t: Quæsívi resíduum annórum meórum. * Dixi: Non vidébo Dóminum Deum in terra vivéntium.

content.latin: 38:12 Non aspíciam hóminem ultra, * et habitatórem quiétis.
content.english: 38:12 I shall behold man no more, * nor the inhabitant of rest.

segments.t: Non aspíciam hóminem ultra, * et habitatórem quiétis.

content.latin: 38:13 Generátio mea abláta est, et convolúta est a me, * quasi tabernáculum pastórum.
content.english: 38:13 My generation is at an end, and it is rolled away from me, * as a shepherd’s tent.

segments.t: Generátio mea abláta est, et convolúta est a me, * quasi tabernáculum pastórum.

content.latin: 38:14 Præcísa est velut a texénte, vita mea: dum adhuc ordírer, succídit me: * de mane usque ad vésperam fínies me.
content.english: 38:14 My life is cut off, as by a weaver: whilst I was yet but beginning, he cut me off: * from morning even to night thou wilt make an end of me.

segments.t: Præcísa est velut a texénte, vita mea: dum adhuc ordírer, succídit me: * de mane usque ad vésperam fínies me.

content.latin: 38:15 Sperábam usque ad mane, * quasi leo sic contrívit ómnia ossa mea:
content.english: 38:15 I hoped till morning, * as a lion so hath he broken all my bones:

segments.t: Sperábam usque ad mane, * quasi leo sic contrívit ómnia ossa mea:

content.latin: 38:16 De mane usque ad vésperam fínies me: * sicut pullus hirúndinis sic clamábo, meditábor ut colúmba:
content.english: 38:16 From morning even to night thou wilt make an end of me. * I will cry like a young swallow, I will meditate like a dove:

segments.t: De mane usque ad vésperam fínies me: * sicut pullus hirúndinis sic clamábo, meditábor ut colúmba:

content.latin: 38:17 Attenuáti sunt óculi mei, * suspiciéntes in excélsum.
content.english: 38:17 My eyes are weakened * looking upward:

segments.t: Attenuáti sunt óculi mei, * suspiciéntes in excélsum.

content.latin: 38:18 Dómine, vim pátior, respónde pro me. * Quid dicam, aut quid respondébit mihi, cum ipse fécerit?
content.english: 38:18 Lord, I suffer violence, answer thou for me. * What shall I say, or what shall he answer for me, whereas he himself hath done it?

segments.t: Dómine, vim pátior, respónde pro me. * Quid dicam, aut quid respondébit mihi, cum ipse fécerit?

content.latin: 38:19 Recogitábo tibi omnes annos meos * in amaritúdine ánimæ meæ.
content.english: 38:19 I will recount to thee all my years * in the bitterness of my soul.

segments.t: Recogitábo tibi omnes annos meos * in amaritúdine ánimæ meæ.

content.latin: 38:20 Dómine, si sic vívitur, et in tálibus vita spíritus mei, corrípies me, et vivificábis me. * Ecce, in pace amaritúdo mea amaríssima:
content.english: 38:20 O Lord, if man’s life be such, and the life of my spirit be in such things as these, thou shalt correct me, and make me to live. * Behold in peace is my bitterness most bitter:

segments.t: Dómine, si sic vívitur, et in tálibus vita spíritus mei, corrípies me, et vivificábis me. * Ecce, in pace amaritúdo mea amaríssima:

content.latin: 38:21 Tu autem eruísti ánimam meam ut non períret: * proiecísti post tergum tuum ómnia peccáta mea.
content.english: 38:21 But thou hast delivered my soul that it should not perish, * thou hast cast all my sins behind thy back.

segments.t: Tu autem eruísti ánimam meam ut non períret: * proiecísti post tergum tuum ómnia peccáta mea.

content.latin: 38:22 Quia non inférnus confitébitur tibi, neque mors laudábit te: * non exspectábunt qui descéndunt in lacum, veritátem tuam.
content.english: 38:22 For hell shall not confess to thee, neither shall death praise thee: * nor shall they that go down into the pit, look for thy truth.

segments.t: Quia non inférnus confitébitur tibi, neque mors laudábit te: * non exspectábunt qui descéndunt in lacum, veritátem tuam.

content.latin: 38:23 Vivens vivens ipse confitébitur tibi, sicut et ego hódie: * pater fíliis notam fáciet veritátem tuam.
content.english: 38:23 The living, the living, he shall give praise to thee, as I do this day: * the father shall make thy truth known to the children.

segments.t: Vivens vivens ipse confitébitur tibi, sicut et ego hódie: * pater fíliis notam fáciet veritátem tuam.

content.latin: 38:24 Dómine, salvum me fac * et psalmos nostros cantábimus cunctis diébus vitæ nostræ in domo Dómini.
content.english: 38:24 O Lord, save me, and we will sing our psalms all the days of our life * in the house of the Lord.

segments.t: Dómine, salvum me fac * et psalmos nostros cantábimus cunctis diébus vitæ nostræ in domo Dómini.

content.english: 150:1 Praise ye the Lord in his holy places: * praise ye him in the firmament of his power.

content.latin: 1:68 Benedíctus ✠ Dóminus, Deus Israël: * quia visitávit, et fecit redemptiónem plebis suæ:
content.english: 1:68 Blessed be the Lord ✠ God of Israel; * because he hath visited and wrought the redemption of his people:

segments.t: Benedíctus ✠ Dóminus, Deus Israël: * quia visitávit, et fecit redemptiónem plebis suæ:

content.latin: 1:69 Et eréxit cornu salútis nobis: * in domo David, púeri sui.
content.english: 1:69 And hath raised up an horn of salvation to us, * in the house of David his servant:

segments.t: Et eréxit cornu salútis nobis: * in domo David, púeri sui.

content.latin: 1:70 Sicut locútus est per os sanctórum, * qui a sǽculo sunt, prophetárum eius:
content.english: 1:70 As he spoke by the mouth of his holy Prophets, * who are from the beginning:

segments.t: Sicut locútus est per os sanctórum, * qui a sǽculo sunt, prophetárum eius:

content.latin: 1:71 Salútem ex inimícis nostris, * et de manu ómnium, qui odérunt nos.
content.english: 1:71 Salvation from our enemies, * and from the hand of all that hate us:

segments.t: Salútem ex inimícis nostris, * et de manu ómnium, qui odérunt nos.

content.latin: 1:72 Ad faciéndam misericórdiam cum pátribus nostris: * et memorári testaménti sui sancti.
content.english: 1:72 To perform mercy to our fathers, * and to remember his holy testament,

segments.t: Ad faciéndam misericórdiam cum pátribus nostris: * et memorári testaménti sui sancti.

content.latin: 1:73 Iusiurándum, quod iurávit ad Ábraham patrem nostrum, * datúrum se nobis:
content.english: 1:73 The oath, which he swore to Abraham our father, * that he would grant to us,

segments.t: Iusiurándum, quod iurávit ad Ábraham patrem nostrum, * datúrum se nobis:

content.latin: 1:74 Ut sine timóre, de manu inimicórum nostrórum liberáti, * serviámus illi.
content.english: 1:74 That being delivered from the hand of our enemies, * we may serve him without fear,

segments.t: Ut sine timóre, de manu inimicórum nostrórum liberáti, * serviámus illi.

content.latin: 1:75 In sanctitáte, et iustítia coram ipso, * ómnibus diébus nostris.
content.english: 1:75 In holiness and justice before him, * all our days.

segments.t: In sanctitáte, et iustítia coram ipso, * ómnibus diébus nostris.

content.latin: 1:76 Et tu, puer, Prophéta Altíssimi vocáberis: * præíbis enim ante fáciem Dómini, paráre vias eius:
content.english: 1:76 And thou, child, shalt be called the prophet of the Highest: * for thou shalt go before the face of the Lord to prepare his ways:

segments.t: Et tu, puer, Prophéta Altíssimi vocáberis: * præíbis enim ante fáciem Dómini, paráre vias eius:

content.latin: 1:77 Ad dandam sciéntiam salútis plebi eius: * in remissiónem peccatórum eórum:
content.english: 1:77 To give knowledge of salvation to his people, * unto the remission of their sins:

segments.t: Ad dandam sciéntiam salútis plebi eius: * in remissiónem peccatórum eórum:

content.latin: 1:78 Per víscera misericórdiæ Dei nostri: * in quibus visitávit nos, óriens ex alto:
content.english: 1:78 Through the bowels of the mercy of our God, * in which the Orient from on high hath visited us:

segments.t: Per víscera misericórdiæ Dei nostri: * in quibus visitávit nos, óriens ex alto:

content.latin: 1:79 Illumináre his, qui in ténebris, et in umbra mortis sedent: * ad dirigéndos pedes nostros in viam pacis.
content.english: 1:79 To enlighten them that sit in darkness, and in the shadow of death: * to direct our feet into the way of peace.

segments.t: Illumináre his, qui in ténebris, et in umbra mortis sedent: * ad dirigéndos pedes nostros in viam pacis.

content.latin: Pater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum: advéniat regnum tuum: fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum cotidiánum da nobis hódie: et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris:
content.english: Our Father, who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us.

content.latin: Fidélium, Deus, ómnium Cónditor et Redémptor, animábus famulórum famularúmque tuárum remissiónem cunctórum tríbue peccatórum: ut indulgéntiam, quam semper optavérunt, piis supplicatiónibus consequántur:
content.english: O God, who art thyself at once the Maker and the Redeemer of all thy faithful ones, grant unto the souls of thy servants and handmaids remission of all their sins, making of our entreaties unto our great Father a mean whereby they may have that forgiveness which they have ever hoped for.

content.english: 87:3 Let my prayer come in before thee: * incline thy ear to my petition.

segments.t: Intret in conspéctu tuo orátio mea: * inclína aurem tuam ad precem meam:

content.latin: 87:4 Quia repléta est malis ánima mea: * et vita mea inférno appropinquávit.
content.english: 87:4 For my soul is filled with evils: * and my life hath drawn nigh to hell.

segments.t: Quia repléta est malis ánima mea: * et vita mea inférno appropinquávit.

content.latin: 87:5 Æstimátus sum cum descendéntibus in lacum: * factus sum sicut homo sine adiutório, inter mórtuos liber.
content.english: 87:5 I am counted among them that go down to the pit: * I am become as a man without help, free among the dead.

segments.t: Æstimátus sum cum descendéntibus in lacum: * factus sum sicut homo sine adiutório, inter mórtuos liber.

content.latin: 87:6 Sicut vulneráti dormiéntes in sepúlcris, quorum non es memor ámplius: * et ipsi de manu tua repúlsi sunt.
content.english: 87:6 Like the slain sleeping in the sepulchres, whom thou rememberest no more: * and they are cast off from thy hand.

segments.t: Sicut vulneráti dormiéntes in sepúlcris, quorum non es memor ámplius: * et ipsi de manu tua repúlsi sunt.

content.latin: 87:7 Posuérunt me in lacu inferióri: * in tenebrósis, et in umbra mortis.
content.english: 87:7 They have laid me in the lower pit: * in the dark places, and in the shadow of death.

segments.t: Posuérunt me in lacu inferióri: * in tenebrósis, et in umbra mortis.

content.latin: 87:8 Super me confirmátus est furor tuus: * et omnes fluctus tuos induxísti super me.
content.english: 87:8 Thy wrath is strong over me: * and all thy waves thou hast brought in upon me.

segments.t: Super me confirmátus est furor tuus: * et omnes fluctus tuos induxísti super me.

content.latin: 87:9 Longe fecísti notos meos a me: * posuérunt me abominatiónem sibi.
content.english: 87:9 Thou hast put away my acquaintance far from me: * they have set me an abomination to themselves.

segments.t: Longe fecísti notos meos a me: * posuérunt me abominatiónem sibi.

content.latin: 87:9 Tráditus sum, et non egrediébar: * óculi mei languérunt præ inópia.
content.english: 87:9 I was delivered up, and came not forth: * my eyes languished through poverty.

segments.t: Tráditus sum, et non egrediébar: * óculi mei languérunt præ inópia.

content.latin: 87:10 Clamávi ad te, Dómine, tota die: * expándi ad te manus meas.
content.english: 87:10 All the day I cried to thee, O Lord: * I stretched out my hands to thee.

segments.t: Clamávi ad te, Dómine, tota die: * expándi ad te manus meas.

content.latin: 87:11 Numquid mórtuis fácies mirabília: * aut médici suscitábunt, et confitebúntur tibi?
content.english: 87:11 Wilt thou shew wonders to the dead? * or shall physicians raise to life, and give praise to thee?

segments.t: Numquid mórtuis fácies mirabília: * aut médici suscitábunt, et confitebúntur tibi?

content.latin: 87:12 Numquid narrábit áliquis in sepúlcro misericórdiam tuam, * et veritátem tuam in perditióne?
content.english: 87:12 Shall any one in the sepulchre declare thy mercy: * and thy truth in destruction?

segments.t: Numquid narrábit áliquis in sepúlcro misericórdiam tuam, * et veritátem tuam in perditióne?

content.latin: 87:13 Numquid cognoscéntur in ténebris mirabília tua, * et iustítia tua in terra obliviónis?
content.english: 87:13 Shall thy wonders be known in the dark; * and thy justice in the land of forgetfulness?

segments.t: Numquid cognoscéntur in ténebris mirabília tua, * et iustítia tua in terra obliviónis?

content.latin: 87:14 Et ego ad te, Dómine, clamávi: * et mane orátio mea prævéniet te.
content.english: 87:14 But I, O Lord, have cried to thee: * and in the morning my prayer shall prevent thee.

segments.t: Et ego ad te, Dómine, clamávi: * et mane orátio mea prævéniet te.

content.latin: 87:15 Ut quid, Dómine, repéllis oratiónem meam: * avértis fáciem tuam a me?
content.english: 87:15 Lord, why castest thou off my prayer: * why turnest thou away thy face from me?

segments.t: Ut quid, Dómine, repéllis oratiónem meam: * avértis fáciem tuam a me?

content.latin: 87:16 Pauper sum ego, et in labóribus a iuventúte mea: * exaltátus autem, humiliátus sum et conturbátus.
content.english: 87:16 I am poor, and in labours from my youth: * and being exalted have been humbled and troubled.

segments.t: Pauper sum ego, et in labóribus a iuventúte mea: * exaltátus autem, humiliátus sum et conturbátus.

content.latin: 87:17 In me transiérunt iræ tuæ: * et terróres tui conturbavérunt me.
content.english: 87:17 Thy wrath hath come upon me: * and thy terrors have troubled me.

segments.t: In me transiérunt iræ tuæ: * et terróres tui conturbavérunt me.

content.latin: 87:18 Circumdedérunt me sicut aqua tota die: * circumdedérunt me simul.
content.english: 87:18 They have come round about me like water all the day: * they have compassed me about together.

segments.t: Circumdedérunt me sicut aqua tota die: * circumdedérunt me simul.

content.latin: 87:19 Elongásti a me amícum et próximum: * et notos meos a miséria.
content.english: 87:19 Friend and neighbour thou hast put far from me: * and my acquaintance, because of misery.

segments.t: Elongásti a me amícum et próximum: * et notos meos a miséria.

content.latin: ℣. Réquiem ætérnam * dona eis, Dómine.
content.english: ℣. Eternal rest * grant unto them, O Lord.

segments.t: Réquiem ætérnam * dona eis, Dómine.

content.latin: ℟. Et lux perpétua * lúceat eis.
content.english: ℟. And let perpetual light * shine upon them.

segments.t: Et lux perpétua * lúceat eis.

content.latin: Psalmus 27 [2]
content.english: Psalm 27 [2]

segments.t: Psalmus 27

content.latin: 27:1 Ad te, Dómine, clamábo, Deus meus, ne síleas a me: * nequándo táceas a me, et assimilábor descendéntibus in lacum.
content.english: 27:1 Unto thee will I cry, O Lord: my God, be not thou silent to me: * lest if thou be silent to me, I become like them that go down into the pit.

segments.t: Ad te, Dómine, clamábo, Deus meus, ne síleas a me: * nequándo táceas a me, et assimilábor descendéntibus in lacum.

content.latin: 27:2 Exáudi, Dómine, vocem deprecatiónis meæ dum oro ad te: * dum extóllo manus meas ad templum sanctum tuum.
content.english: 27:2 Hear, O Lord, the voice of my supplication, when I pray to thee; * when I lift up my hands to thy holy temple.

segments.t: Exáudi, Dómine, vocem deprecatiónis meæ dum oro ad te: * dum extóllo manus meas ad templum sanctum tuum.

content.latin: 27:3 Ne simul trahas me cum peccatóribus: * et cum operántibus iniquitátem ne perdas me.
content.english: 27:3 Draw me not away together with the wicked; * and with the workers of iniquity destroy me not:

segments.t: Ne simul trahas me cum peccatóribus: * et cum operántibus iniquitátem ne perdas me.

content.latin: 27:3 Qui loquúntur pacem cum próximo suo, * mala autem in córdibus eórum.
content.english: 27:3 Who speak peace with their neighbour, * but evils are in their hearts.

segments.t: Qui loquúntur pacem cum próximo suo, * mala autem in córdibus eórum.

content.latin: 27:4 Da illis secúndum ópera eórum, * et secúndum nequítiam adinventiónum ipsórum.
content.english: 27:4 Give them according to their works, * and according to the wickedness of their inventions.

segments.t: Da illis secúndum ópera eórum, * et secúndum nequítiam adinventiónum ipsórum.

content.latin: 27:4 Secúndum ópera mánuum eórum tríbue illis: * redde retributiónem eórum ipsis.
content.english: 27:4 According to the works of their hands give thou to them: * render to them their reward.

segments.t: Secúndum ópera mánuum eórum tríbue illis: * redde retributiónem eórum ipsis.

content.latin: 27:5 Quóniam non intellexérunt ópera Dómini, et in ópera mánuum eius * déstrues illos, et non ædificábis eos.
content.english: 27:5 Because they have not understood the works of the Lord, and the operations of his hands: * thou shalt destroy them, and shalt not build them up.

segments.t: Quóniam non intellexérunt ópera Dómini, et in ópera mánuum eius * déstrues illos, et non ædificábis eos.

content.latin: 27:6 Benedíctus Dóminus: * quóniam exaudívit vocem deprecatiónis meæ.
content.english: 27:6 Blessed be the Lord, * for he hath heard the voice of my supplication.

segments.t: Benedíctus Dóminus: * quóniam exaudívit vocem deprecatiónis meæ.

content.latin: 27:7 Dóminus adiútor meus, et protéctor meus: * in ipso sperávit cor meum, et adiútus sum.
content.english: 27:7 The Lord is my helper and my protector: * in him hath my heart confided, and I have been helped.

segments.t: Dóminus adiútor meus, et protéctor meus: * in ipso sperávit cor meum, et adiútus sum.

content.latin: 27:7 Et reflóruit caro mea: * et ex voluntáte mea confitébor ei.
content.english: 27:7 And my flesh hath flourished again, * and with my will I will give praise to him.

segments.t: Et reflóruit caro mea: * et ex voluntáte mea confitébor ei.

content.latin: 27:8 Dóminus fortitúdo plebis suæ: * et protéctor salvatiónum Christi sui est.
content.english: 27:8 The Lord is the strength of his people, * and the protector of the salvation of his anointed.

segments.t: Dóminus fortitúdo plebis suæ: * et protéctor salvatiónum Christi sui est.

content.latin: 27:9 Salvum fac pópulum tuum, Dómine, et bénedic hereditáti tuæ: * et rege eos, et extólle illos usque in ætérnum.
content.english: 27:9 Save, O Lord, thy people, and bless thy inheritance: * and rule them and exalt them for ever.

segments.t: Salvum fac pópulum tuum, Dómine, et bénedic hereditáti tuæ: * et rege eos, et extólle illos usque in ætérnum.

content.latin: ℣. Réquiem ætérnam * dona eis, Dómine.
content.english: ℣. Eternal rest * grant unto them, O Lord.

segments.t: Réquiem ætérnam * dona eis, Dómine.

content.latin: ℟. Et lux perpétua * lúceat eis.
content.english: ℟. And let perpetual light * shine upon them.

segments.t: Et lux perpétua * lúceat eis.

content.latin: Psalmus 31 [3]
content.english: Psalm 31 [3]

segments.t: Psalmus 31

content.latin: 31:1 Beáti quorum remíssæ sunt iniquitátes: * et quorum tecta sunt peccáta.
content.english: 31:1 Blessed are those whose iniquities are forgiven * and whose sins are covered.

segments.t: Beáti quorum remíssæ sunt iniquitátes: * et quorum tecta sunt peccáta.

content.latin: 31:2 Beátus vir, cui non imputávit Dóminus peccátum, * nec est in spíritu eius dolus.
content.english: 31:2 Blessed is the man to whom the Lord hath not imputed sin, * and in whose spirit there is no guile.

segments.t: Beátus vir, cui non imputávit Dóminus peccátum, * nec est in spíritu eius dolus.

content.latin: 31:3 Quóniam tácui, inveteravérunt ossa mea, * dum clamárem tota die.
content.english: 31:3 Because I was silent my bones grew old; * whilst I cried out all the day long.

segments.t: Quóniam tácui, inveteravérunt ossa mea, * dum clamárem tota die.

content.latin: 31:4 Quóniam die ac nocte graváta est super me manus tua: * convérsus sum in ærúmna mea, dum confígitur spina.
content.english: 31:4 For day and night thy hand was heavy upon me: * I am turned in my anguish, whilst the thorn is fastened.

segments.t: Quóniam die ac nocte graváta est super me manus tua: * convérsus sum in ærúmna mea, dum confígitur spina.

content.latin: 31:5 Delíctum meum cógnitum tibi feci: * et iniustítiam meam non abscóndi.
content.english: 31:5 I have acknowledged my sin to thee, * and my injustice I have not concealed.

segments.t: Delíctum meum cógnitum tibi feci: * et iniustítiam meam non abscóndi.

content.latin: 31:5 Dixi: Confitébor advérsum me iniustítiam meam Dómino: * et tu remisísti impietátem peccáti mei.
content.english: 31:5 I said I will confess against myself my injustice to the Lord: * and thou hast forgiven the wickedness of my sin.

segments.t: Dixi: Confitébor advérsum me iniustítiam meam Dómino: * et tu remisísti impietátem peccáti mei.

content.latin: 31:6 Pro hac orábit ad te omnis sanctus, * in témpore opportúno.
content.english: 31:6 For this shall every one that is holy pray to thee * in a seasonable time.

segments.t: Pro hac orábit ad te omnis sanctus, * in témpore opportúno.

content.latin: 31:6 Verúmtamen in dilúvio aquárum multárum, * ad eum non approximábunt.
content.english: 31:6 And yet in a flood of many waters, * they shall not come nigh unto him.

segments.t: Verúmtamen in dilúvio aquárum multárum, * ad eum non approximábunt.

content.latin: 31:7 Tu es refúgium meum a tribulatióne, quæ circúmdedit me: * exsultátio mea, érue me a circumdántibus me.
content.english: 31:7 Thou art my refuge from the trouble which hath encompassed me: * my joy, deliver me from them that surround me.

segments.t: Tu es refúgium meum a tribulatióne, quæ circúmdedit me: * exsultátio mea, érue me a circumdántibus me.

content.latin: 31:8 Intelléctum tibi dabo, et ínstruam te in via hac, qua gradiéris: * firmábo super te óculos meos.
content.english: 31:8 I will give thee understanding, and I will instruct thee in this way, in which thou shalt go: * I will fix my eyes upon thee.

segments.t: Intelléctum tibi dabo, et ínstruam te in via hac, qua gradiéris: * firmábo super te óculos meos.

content.latin: 31:9 Nolíte fíeri sicut equus et mulus, * quibus non est intelléctus.
content.english: 31:9 Do not become like the horse and the mule, * who have no understanding.

segments.t: Nolíte fíeri sicut equus et mulus, * quibus non est intelléctus.

content.latin: 31:9 In camo et freno maxíllas eórum constrínge, * qui non appróximant ad te.
content.english: 31:9 With bit and bridle bind fast their jaws, * who come not near unto thee.

segments.t: In camo et freno maxíllas eórum constrínge, * qui non appróximant ad te.

content.latin: 31:10 Multa flagélla peccatóris, * sperántem autem in Dómino misericórdia circúmdabit.
content.english: 31:10 Many are the scourges of the sinner, * but mercy shall encompass him that hopeth in the Lord.

segments.t: Multa flagélla peccatóris, * sperántem autem in Dómino misericórdia circúmdabit.

content.latin: 31:11 Lætámini in Dómino et exsultáte, iusti, * et gloriámini, omnes recti corde.
content.english: 31:11 Be glad in the Lord, and rejoice, ye just, * and glory, all ye right of heart.

segments.t: Lætámini in Dómino et exsultáte, iusti, * et gloriámini, omnes recti corde.

content.latin: ℣. Réquiem ætérnam * dona eis, Dómine.
content.english: ℣. Eternal rest * grant unto them, O Lord.

segments.t: Réquiem ætérnam * dona eis, Dómine.

content.latin: ℟. Et lux perpétua * lúceat eis.
content.english: ℟. And let perpetual light * shine upon them.

segments.t: Et lux perpétua * lúceat eis.

content.latin: Pater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum: advéniat regnum tuum: fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum cotidiánum da nobis hódie: et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris:
content.english: Our Father, who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us.

content.latin: ℣. Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
content.english: ℣. And lead us not into temptation:

segments.t: Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:

content.latin: ℟. Sed líbera nos a malo.
content.english: ℟. But deliver us from evil.

segments.t: Sed líbera nos a malo.

content.latin: ℣. A porta ínferi.
content.english: ℣. From the gates of hell.

segments.t: A porta ínferi.

content.latin: ℟. Erue, Dómine, ánimas eórum.
content.english: ℟. Deliver their souls, O Lord!

segments.t: Erue, Dómine, ánimas eórum.

content.latin: ℣. Requiéscant in pace.
content.english: ℣. May they rest in peace.

segments.t: Requiéscant in pace.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.

content.latin: ℣. Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.
content.english: ℣. O Lord, hear my prayer.

segments.t: Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.

content.latin: ℟. Et clamor meus ad te véniat.
content.english: ℟. And let my cry come unto thee.

segments.t: Et clamor meus ad te véniat.

content.latin: secunda Domine, exaudi omittitur
content.english: skip second O Lord, hear my prayer

segments.t: secunda Domine, exaudi omittitur

content.latin: Orémus.
content.english: Let us pray.

content.latin: Súpplices, Dómine, pro animábus ómnium famulórum famularúmque tuárum preces effúndimus: ut, quidquid conversatióne contraxérunt humána, clemens indúlgeas, et pœnis eórum finem benígnus impónas.
content.english: We suppliants, O Lord, pour forth our prayers for the souls of all thy servants and handmaids, that thou wouldst mercifully pardon whatsoever they have committed through human frailty, and graciously vouchsafe to deliver them from the pains of purgatory.

content.latin: Per Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: Through Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.

content.latin: Hac die Commemorátio ómnium Fidélium Defunctórum; in qua commúnis pia Mater Ecclésia, postquam univérsos fílios suos iam in cælo lætántes cóngruis stúduit celebráre præcóniis, mox et omnes adhuc in Purgatório geméntes válidis apud Dóminum et Sponsum Christum satágit suffrágiis adiuváre, ut quam cítius váleant ad societátem supernórum cívium perveníre.
content.english: On this day, the Commemoration of all the Faithful Departed, on which day Holy Church, their common Mother, after due diligence to celebrate with fitting praise all her children who now rejoice in heaven, doth strive also to assist by her prayers all them that suffer still in Purgatory, which are of avail before Christ, her Lord and Spouse, in order that as speedily as possible they may join the society of the citizens on high.

content.latin: Tértio Nonas Novémbris Luna vicésima tértia Anno Dómini 2026
content.english: On the morrow we keep in England the feast of the holy Virgin and martyr Winefrid.

content.latin: Medioláni natális sancti Cároli Borromǽi Cardinális, Epíscopi Mediolanénsis et Confessóris, quem, sanctitáte conspícuum et miráculis clarum, Paulus Papa Quintus in sanctórum númerum rétulit. Ipsíus tamen festívitas sequénti die celebrátur.
content.english: November 3rd 2026, the 23rd day of the Moon, were also born into the better life:

content.latin: Eódem die natális quoque sancti Quarti, Apostolórum discípuli.
content.english: Holy Quartus, the disciple of the Apostles.

content.latin: Vitérbii sanctórum Mártyrum Valentíni Presbýteri, et Hilárii Diáconi, qui, in persecutióne Maximiáni, ob Christi fidem, cum saxi póndere in Tíberim præcipitáti et inde ab Angelo divínitus erépti, demum, abscíssis cervícibus, corónam martýrii percepérunt.
content.english: At Caesarea, in Cappadocia, the holy martyrs Germanus, Theophilus, Caesarius, and Vitalis, who bore a noble testimony in the persecution under the Emperor Decius.

content.latin: Cæsaréæ, in Cappadócia, sanctórum Mártyrum Germáni, Theóphili, Cæsárii et Vitális; qui, in persecutióne Deciána, óptime duxérunt martýrium.
content.english: At Saragossa, countless holy martyrs, who wondrously laid down their lives for Christ's sake under Dacian, President of Spain, (in the year 304.)

content.latin: Cæsaraugústæ, in Hispánia, sanctórum innumerabílium Mártyrum, qui, sub Hispaniárum Prǽside Daciáno, mirabíliter occubuérunt pro Christo.
content.english: At Viterbo, the holy martyrs Valentine the Priest and Hilary the Deacon, who, in the persecution under the Emperor Maximian, were for Christ's faith's sake cast into the Tiber weighted with stones, but by the will of God were thence delivered by an Angel, and received the crown of martyrdom by being beheaded.

content.latin: In Anglia sanctæ Wenefrídæ, Vírginis et Mártyris.
content.english: At the monastery of Clairvaux, (in the year 1148,) holy Maleachlan, Archbishop of Armagh, in Ireland, who in his time shone with many graces, and whose life hath been written by the holy Abbot Bernard.

content.latin: In monastério Clarævallénsi, in Gállia, deposítio sancti Malachíæ, Connerthénsis in Hibérnia Epíscopi, qui multis virtútibus suo témpore cláruit; cuius vitam sanctus Bernárdus Abbas conscrípsit.
content.english: On the same day, (in the year 727,) holy Hubert, Bishop of Tongres.

content.latin: Eódem die sancti Hubérti, Tungrénsis Epíscopi.
content.english: At Vienne, (in the sixth century,) holy Domnus, Bishop (of that see.)

content.latin: Viénnæ, in Gállia, sancti Domni, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
content.english: Likewise (in the year 755,) holy Pirmin, Bishop of Meaux.

content.latin: Item deposítio sancti Pirmíni, Meldénsis Epíscopi.
content.english: At Urgel, in Spain, holy Hermengaudus, Bishop (of that see.)

content.latin: Urgéllæ, in Hispánia Tarraconénsi, sancti Hermengáudii Epíscopi.
content.english: At Rome, holy Sylvia, the mother of holy Pope Gregory.

content.latin: Romæ sanctæ Sílviæ, matris sancti Gregórii Papæ.
content.english: ℣. And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.

content.latin: ℣. Et álibi aliórum plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum et Confessórum, atque sanctárum Vírginum.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

segments.t: Et álibi aliórum plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum et Confessórum, atque sanctárum Vírginum.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℣. The just shall be in everlasting remembrance.

segments.t: Deo grátias.

content.latin: ℣. In memória ætérna erunt iusti.
content.english: ℟. They will not fear from hearing evil.

segments.t: In memória ætérna erunt iusti.

content.latin: ℟. Ab auditióne mala non timébunt.
content.english: Let us pray.

segments.t: Ab auditióne mala non timébunt.

content.latin: Orémus.
content.english: O God the giver of pardon, and the lover of human salvation, we beseech thy clemency: that thou grant the brethren of our congregation, kinsfolk, and benefactors, which are departed out of this world, blessed Mary ever Virgin making intercession with all the saints, to come to the fellowship of eternal blessedness. Through Christ our Lord.

content.latin: Deus, véniæ largítor et humánæ salútis amátor: quǽsumus cleméntiam tuam; ut ánimas ómnium fidélium qui ex hoc sǽculo transiérunt, beáta María semper Vírgine intercedénte cum ómnibus Sanctis tuis, ad perpétuæ beatitúdinis consórtium perveníre concédas. Per Christum Dóminum nostrum.

Psalmus 37(1-11)

content.latin: 37:2 Dómine, ne in furóre tuo árguas me, * neque in ira tua corrípias me.
content.english: 37:2 Rebuke me not, O Lord, in thy indignation; * nor chastise me in thy wrath.

segments.t: Dómine, ne in furóre tuo árguas me, * neque in ira tua corrípias me.

content.latin: 37:3 Quóniam sagíttæ tuæ infíxæ sunt mihi: * et confirmásti super me manum tuam.
content.english: 37:3 For thy arrows are fastened in me: * and thy hand hath been strong upon me.

segments.t: Quóniam sagíttæ tuæ infíxæ sunt mihi: * et confirmásti super me manum tuam.

content.latin: 37:4 Non est sánitas in carne mea a fácie iræ tuæ: * non est pax óssibus meis a fácie peccatórum meórum.
content.english: 37:4 There is no health in my flesh, because of thy wrath: * there is no peace for my bones, because of my sins.

segments.t: Non est sánitas in carne mea a fácie iræ tuæ: * non est pax óssibus meis a fácie peccatórum meórum.

content.latin: 37:5 Quóniam iniquitátes meæ supergréssæ sunt caput meum: * et sicut onus grave gravátæ sunt super me.
content.english: 37:5 For my iniquities are gone over my head: * and as a heavy burden are become heavy upon me.

segments.t: Quóniam iniquitátes meæ supergréssæ sunt caput meum: * et sicut onus grave gravátæ sunt super me.

content.latin: 37:6 Putruérunt et corrúptæ sunt cicatríces meæ, * a fácie insipiéntiæ meæ.
content.english: 37:6 My sores are putrified and corrupted, * because of my foolishness.

segments.t: Putruérunt et corrúptæ sunt cicatríces meæ, * a fácie insipiéntiæ meæ.

content.latin: 37:7 Miser factus sum, et curvátus sum usque in finem: * tota die contristátus ingrediébar.
content.english: 37:7 I am become miserable, and am bowed down even to the end: * I walked sorrowful all the day long.

segments.t: Miser factus sum, et curvátus sum usque in finem: * tota die contristátus ingrediébar.

content.latin: 37:8 Quóniam lumbi mei impléti sunt illusiónibus: * et non est sánitas in carne mea.
content.english: 37:8 For my loins are filled with illusions; * and there is no health in my flesh.

segments.t: Quóniam lumbi mei impléti sunt illusiónibus: * et non est sánitas in carne mea.

content.latin: 37:9 Afflíctus sum, et humiliátus sum nimis: * rugiébam a gémitu cordis mei.
content.english: 37:9 I am afflicted and humbled exceedingly: * I roared with the groaning of my heart.

segments.t: Afflíctus sum, et humiliátus sum nimis: * rugiébam a gémitu cordis mei.

content.latin: 37:10 Dómine, ante te omne desidérium meum: * et gémitus meus a te non est abscónditus.
content.english: 37:10 Lord, all my desire is before thee, * and my groaning is not hidden from thee.

segments.t: Dómine, ante te omne desidérium meum: * et gémitus meus a te non est abscónditus.

content.latin: 37:11 Cor meum conturbátum est, derelíquit me virtus mea: * et lumen oculórum meórum, et ipsum non est mecum.
content.english: 37:11 My heart is troubled, my strength hath left me, * and the light of my eyes itself is not with me.

segments.t: Cor meum conturbátum est, derelíquit me virtus mea: * et lumen oculórum meórum, et ipsum non est mecum.

Psalmus 37(12-23)

content.latin: 37:12 Amíci mei, et próximi mei * advérsum me appropinquavérunt, et stetérunt.
content.english: 37:12 My friends and my neighbours * have drawn near, and stood against me.

segments.t: Amíci mei, et próximi mei * advérsum me appropinquavérunt, et stetérunt.

content.latin: 37:12 Et qui iuxta me erant, de longe stetérunt: * et vim faciébant qui quærébant ánimam meam.
content.english: 37:12 And they that were near me stood afar off: * and they that sought my soul used violence.

segments.t: Et qui iuxta me erant, de longe stetérunt: * et vim faciébant qui quærébant ánimam meam.

content.latin: 37:13 Et qui inquirébant mala mihi, locúti sunt vanitátes: * et dolos tota die meditabántur.
content.english: 37:13 And they that sought evils to me spoke vain things, * and studied deceits all the day long.

segments.t: Et qui inquirébant mala mihi, locúti sunt vanitátes: * et dolos tota die meditabántur.

content.latin: 37:14 Ego autem tamquam surdus non audiébam: * et sicut mutus non apériens os suum.
content.english: 37:14 But I, as a deaf man, heard not: * and as a dumb man not opening his mouth.

segments.t: Ego autem tamquam surdus non audiébam: * et sicut mutus non apériens os suum.

content.latin: 37:15 Et factus sum sicut homo non áudiens: * et non habens in ore suo redargutiónes.
content.english: 37:15 And I became as a man that heareth not: * and that hath no reproofs in his mouth.

segments.t: Et factus sum sicut homo non áudiens: * et non habens in ore suo redargutiónes.

content.latin: 37:16 Quóniam in te, Dómine, sperávi: * tu exáudies me, Dómine, Deus meus.
content.english: 37:16 For in thee, O Lord, have I hoped: * thou wilt hear me, O Lord my God.

segments.t: Quóniam in te, Dómine, sperávi: * tu exáudies me, Dómine, Deus meus.

content.latin: 37:17 Quia dixi: Nequándo supergáudeant mihi inimíci mei: * et dum commovéntur pedes mei, super me magna locúti sunt.
content.english: 37:17 For I said: Lest at any time my enemies rejoice over me: * and whilst my feet are moved, they speak great things against me.

segments.t: Quia dixi: Nequándo supergáudeant mihi inimíci mei: * et dum commovéntur pedes mei, super me magna locúti sunt.

content.latin: 37:18 Quóniam ego in flagélla parátus sum: * et dolor meus in conspéctu meo semper.
content.english: 37:18 For I am ready for scourges: * and my sorrow is continually before me.

segments.t: Quóniam ego in flagélla parátus sum: * et dolor meus in conspéctu meo semper.

content.latin: 37:19 Quóniam iniquitátem meam annuntiábo: * et cogitábo pro peccáto meo.
content.english: 37:19 For I will declare my iniquity: * and I will think for my sin.

segments.t: Quóniam iniquitátem meam annuntiábo: * et cogitábo pro peccáto meo.

content.latin: 37:20 Inimíci autem mei vivunt, et confirmáti sunt super me: * et multiplicáti sunt qui odérunt me iníque.
content.english: 37:20 But my enemies live, and are stronger than I: * and they that hate me wrongfully are multiplied.

segments.t: Inimíci autem mei vivunt, et confirmáti sunt super me: * et multiplicáti sunt qui odérunt me iníque.

content.latin: 37:21 Qui retríbuunt mala pro bonis, detrahébant mihi: * quóniam sequébar bonitátem.
content.english: 37:21 They that render evil for good, have detracted me, * because I followed goodness.

segments.t: Qui retríbuunt mala pro bonis, detrahébant mihi: * quóniam sequébar bonitátem.

content.latin: 37:22 Ne derelínquas me, Dómine, Deus meus: * ne discésseris a me.
content.english: 37:22 Forsake me not, O Lord my God: * do not thou depart from me.

segments.t: Ne derelínquas me, Dómine, Deus meus: * ne discésseris a me.

content.latin: 37:23 Inténde in adiutórium meum, * Dómine, Deus, salútis meæ.
content.english: 37:23 Attend unto my help, * O Lord, the God of my salvation.

segments.t: Inténde in adiutórium meum, * Dómine, Deus, salútis meæ.

content.english: Psalm 55 [3]

segments.t: Psalmus 55

content.latin: 55:2 Miserére mei, Deus, quóniam conculcávit me homo: * tota die impúgnans tribulávit me.
content.english: 55:2 Have mercy on me, O God, for man hath trodden me under foot; * all the day long he hath afflicted me fighting against me.

segments.t: Miserére mei, Deus, quóniam conculcávit me homo: * tota die impúgnans tribulávit me.

content.latin: 55:3 Conculcavérunt me inimíci mei tota die: * quóniam multi bellántes advérsum me.
content.english: 55:3 My enemies have trodden on me all the day long; * for they are many that make war against me.

segments.t: Conculcavérunt me inimíci mei tota die: * quóniam multi bellántes advérsum me.

content.latin: 55:4 Ab altitúdine diéi timébo: * ego vero in te sperábo.
content.english: 55:4 From the height of the day I shall fear: * but I will trust in thee.

segments.t: Ab altitúdine diéi timébo: * ego vero in te sperábo.

content.latin: 55:5 In Deo laudábo sermónes meos, in Deo sperávi: * non timébo quid fáciat mihi caro.
content.english: 55:5 In God I will praise my words, in God I have put my trust: * I will not fear what flesh can do against me.

segments.t: In Deo laudábo sermónes meos, in Deo sperávi: * non timébo quid fáciat mihi caro.

content.latin: 55:6 Tota die verba mea exsecrabántur: * advérsum me omnes cogitatiónes eórum in malum.
content.english: 55:6 All the day long they detested my words: * all their thoughts were against me unto evil.

segments.t: Tota die verba mea exsecrabántur: * advérsum me omnes cogitatiónes eórum in malum.

content.latin: 55:7 Inhabitábunt et abscóndent: * ipsi calcáneum meum observábunt.
content.english: 55:7 They will dwell and hide themselves: * they will watch my heel.

segments.t: Inhabitábunt et abscóndent: * ipsi calcáneum meum observábunt.

content.latin: 55:8 Sicut sustinuérunt ánimam meam, pro níhilo salvos fácies illos: * in ira pópulos confrínges.
content.english: 55:8 As they have waited for my soul, for nothing shalt thou save them: * in thy anger thou shalt break the people in pieces.

segments.t: Sicut sustinuérunt ánimam meam, pro níhilo salvos fácies illos: * in ira pópulos confrínges.

content.latin: 55:9 Deus, vitam meam annuntiávi tibi: * posuísti lácrimas meas in conspéctu tuo.
content.english: 55:9 O God, I have declared to thee my life: * thou hast set my tears in thy sight,

segments.t: Deus, vitam meam annuntiávi tibi: * posuísti lácrimas meas in conspéctu tuo.

content.latin: 55:9 Sicut et in promissióne tua: * tunc converténtur inimíci mei retrórsum:
content.english: 55:9 As also in thy promise. * Then shall my enemies be turned back.

segments.t: Sicut et in promissióne tua: * tunc converténtur inimíci mei retrórsum:

content.latin: 55:10 In quacúmque die invocávero te: * ecce, cognóvi, quóniam Deus meus es.
content.english: 55:10 In what day soever I shall call upon thee, * behold I know thou art my God.

segments.t: In quacúmque die invocávero te: * ecce, cognóvi, quóniam Deus meus es.

content.latin: 55:11 In Deo laudábo verbum, in Dómino laudábo sermónem: * in Deo sperávi, non timébo quid fáciat mihi homo.
content.english: 55:11 In God will I praise the word, in the Lord will I praise his speech. * In God have I hoped, I will not fear what man can do to me.

segments.t: In Deo laudábo verbum, in Dómino laudábo sermónem: * in Deo sperávi, non timébo quid fáciat mihi homo.

content.latin: 55:12 In me sunt, Deus, vota tua, * quæ reddam, laudatiónes tibi.
content.english: 55:12 In me, O God, are vows to thee, * which I will pay, praises to thee:

segments.t: In me sunt, Deus, vota tua, * quæ reddam, laudatiónes tibi.

content.latin: 55:13 Quóniam eripuísti ánimam meam de morte, et pedes meos de lapsu: * ut pláceam coram Deo in lúmine vivéntium.
content.english: 55:13 Because thou hast delivered my soul from death, my feet from falling: * that I may please in the sight of God, in the light of the living.

segments.t: Quóniam eripuísti ánimam meam de morte, et pedes meos de lapsu: * ut pláceam coram Deo in lúmine vivéntium.

content.latin: ℣. Réquiem ætérnam * dona eis, Dómine.
content.english: ℣. Eternal rest * grant unto them, O Lord.

segments.t: Réquiem ætérnam * dona eis, Dómine.

content.english: ℟. And let perpetual light * shine upon them.

content.latin: Pater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum: advéniat regnum tuum: fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum cotidiánum da nobis hódie: et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris:
content.english: Our Father, who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us.

content.latin: ℣. Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
content.english: ℣. And lead us not into temptation:

segments.t: Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:

content.latin: ℟. Sed líbera nos a malo.
content.english: ℟. But deliver us from evil.

segments.t: Sed líbera nos a malo.

content.latin: ℣. A porta ínferi.
content.english: ℣. From the gates of hell.

segments.t: A porta ínferi.

content.latin: ℟. Erue, Dómine, ánimas eórum.
content.english: ℟. Deliver their souls, O Lord!

segments.t: Erue, Dómine, ánimas eórum.

content.latin: ℣. Requiéscant in pace.
content.english: ℣. May they rest in peace.

segments.t: Requiéscant in pace.

content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.

content.latin: ℣. Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.
content.english: ℣. O Lord, hear my prayer.

segments.t: Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.

content.latin: ℟. Et clamor meus ad te véniat.
content.english: ℟. And let my cry come unto thee.

segments.t: Et clamor meus ad te véniat.

content.latin: secunda Domine, exaudi omittitur
content.english: skip second O Lord, hear my prayer

segments.t: secunda Domine, exaudi omittitur

content.latin: Orémus.
content.english: Let us pray.

content.latin: Fidélium, Deus, ómnium Cónditor et Redémptor, animábus famulórum famularúmque tuárum remissiónem cunctórum tríbue peccatórum: ut indulgéntiam, quam semper optavérunt, piis supplicatiónibus consequántur:
content.english: O God, who art thyself at once the Maker and the Redeemer of all thy faithful ones, grant unto the souls of thy servants and handmaids remission of all their sins, making of our entreaties unto our great Father a mean whereby they may have that forgiveness which they have ever hoped for.

content.latin: Qui vivis et regnas cum Deo Patre, in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: Who livest and reignest with God the Father in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, world without end.

content.english: ℟. Amen.

content.latin: 69:2 Deus, in adiutórium meum inténde: * Dómine, ad adiuvándum me festína.
content.english: 69:2 O God, come to my assistance; * O Lord, make haste to help me.

segments.t: Deus, in adiutórium meum inténde: * Dómine, ad adiuvándum me festína.

content.latin: 69:3 Confundántur et revereántur, * qui quærunt ánimam meam.
content.english: 69:3 Let them be confounded and ashamed * that seek my soul:

segments.t: Confundántur et revereántur, * qui quærunt ánimam meam.

content.latin: 69:4 Avertántur retrórsum, et erubéscant, * qui volunt mihi mala.
content.english: 69:4 Let them be turned backward, and blush for shame * that desire evils to me:

segments.t: Avertántur retrórsum, et erubéscant, * qui volunt mihi mala.

content.latin: 69:4 Avertántur statim erubescéntes, * qui dicunt mihi: Euge, euge.
content.english: 69:4 Let them be presently turned away blushing for shame * that say to me: ’T is well, ’t is well.

segments.t: Avertántur statim erubescéntes, * qui dicunt mihi: Euge, euge.

content.latin: 69:5 Exsúltent et læténtur in te omnes qui quærunt te, * et dicant semper: Magnificétur Dóminus: qui díligunt salutáre tuum.
content.english: 69:5 Let all that seek thee rejoice and be glad in thee; * and let such as love thy salvation say always: The Lord be magnified.

segments.t: Exsúltent et læténtur in te omnes qui quærunt te, * et dicant semper: Magnificétur Dóminus: qui díligunt salutáre tuum.

content.latin: 69:6 Ego vero egénus, et pauper sum: * Deus, ádiuva me.
content.english: 69:6 But I am needy and poor; * O God, help me.

segments.t: Ego vero egénus, et pauper sum: * Deus, ádiuva me.

content.latin: 69:6 Adiútor meus, et liberátor meus es tu: * Dómine, ne moréris.
content.english: 69:6 Thou art my helper and my deliverer: * O Lord, make no delay.

segments.t: Adiútor meus, et liberátor meus es tu: * Dómine, ne moréris.

content.english: ℣. Eternal rest * grant unto them, O Lord.

content.english: Psalm 84 [2]

segments.t: Psalmus 84

content.latin: 84:2 Benedixísti, Dómine, terram tuam: * avertísti captivitátem Iacob.
content.english: 84:2 Lord, thou hast blessed thy land: * thou hast turned away the captivity of Jacob.

segments.t: Benedixísti, Dómine, terram tuam: * avertísti captivitátem Iacob.

content.latin: 84:3 Remisísti iniquitátem plebis tuæ: * operuísti ómnia peccáta eórum.
content.english: 84:3 Thou hast forgiven the iniquity of thy people: * thou hast covered all their sins.

segments.t: Remisísti iniquitátem plebis tuæ: * operuísti ómnia peccáta eórum.

content.latin: 84:4 Mitigásti omnem iram tuam: * avertísti ab ira indignatiónis tuæ.
content.english: 84:4 Thou hast mitigated all thy anger: * thou hast turned away from the wrath of thy indignation.

segments.t: Mitigásti omnem iram tuam: * avertísti ab ira indignatiónis tuæ.

content.latin: 84:5 Convérte nos, Deus, salutáris noster: * et avérte iram tuam a nobis.
content.english: 84:5 Convert us, O God our saviour: * and turn off thy anger from us.

segments.t: Convérte nos, Deus, salutáris noster: * et avérte iram tuam a nobis.

content.latin: 84:6 Numquid in ætérnum irascéris nobis? * aut exténdes iram tuam a generatióne in generatiónem?
content.english: 84:6 Wilt thou be angry with us for ever: * or wilt thou extend thy wrath from generation to generation?

segments.t: Numquid in ætérnum irascéris nobis? * aut exténdes iram tuam a generatióne in generatiónem?

content.latin: 84:7 Deus, tu convérsus vivificábis nos: * et plebs tua lætábitur in te.
content.english: 84:7 Thou wilt turn, O God, and bring us to life: * and thy people shall rejoice in thee.

segments.t: Deus, tu convérsus vivificábis nos: * et plebs tua lætábitur in te.

content.latin: 84:8 Osténde nobis, Dómine, misericórdiam tuam: * et salutáre tuum da nobis.
content.english: 84:8 Shew us, O Lord, thy mercy; * and grant us thy salvation.

segments.t: Osténde nobis, Dómine, misericórdiam tuam: * et salutáre tuum da nobis.

content.latin: 84:9 Áudiam quid loquátur in me Dóminus Deus: * quóniam loquétur pacem in plebem suam.
content.english: 84:9 I will hear what the Lord God will speak in me: * for he will speak peace

segments.t: Áudiam quid loquátur in me Dóminus Deus: * quóniam loquétur pacem in plebem suam.

content.latin: 84:9 Et super sanctos suos: * et in eos, qui convertúntur ad cor.
content.english: 84:9 And unto his saints: * and unto them that are converted to the heart.

segments.t: Et super sanctos suos: * et in eos, qui convertúntur ad cor.

content.latin: 84:10 Verúmtamen prope timéntes eum salutáre ipsíus: * ut inhábitet glória in terra nostra.
content.english: 84:10 Surely his salvation is near to them that fear him: * that glory may dwell in our land.

segments.t: Verúmtamen prope timéntes eum salutáre ipsíus: * ut inhábitet glória in terra nostra.

content.latin: 84:11 Misericórdia, et véritas obviavérunt sibi: * iustítia, et pax osculátæ sunt.
content.english: 84:11 Mercy and truth have met each other: * justice and peace have kissed.

segments.t: Misericórdia, et véritas obviavérunt sibi: * iustítia, et pax osculátæ sunt.

content.latin: 84:12 Véritas de terra orta est: * et iustítia de cælo prospéxit.
content.english: 84:12 Truth is sprung out of the earth: * and justice hath looked down from heaven.

segments.t: Véritas de terra orta est: * et iustítia de cælo prospéxit.

content.latin: 84:13 Étenim Dóminus dabit benignitátem: * et terra nostra dabit fructum suum.
content.english: 84:13 For the Lord will give goodness: * and our earth shall yield her fruit.

segments.t: Étenim Dóminus dabit benignitátem: * et terra nostra dabit fructum suum.

content.latin: 84:14 Iustítia ante eum ambulábit: * et ponet in via gressus suos.
content.english: 84:14 Justice shall walk before him: * and shall set his steps in the way.

segments.t: Iustítia ante eum ambulábit: * et ponet in via gressus suos.

content.latin: ℣. Réquiem ætérnam * dona eis, Dómine.
content.english: ℣. Eternal rest * grant unto them, O Lord.

segments.t: Réquiem ætérnam * dona eis, Dómine.

content.latin: ℟. Et lux perpétua * lúceat eis.
content.english: ℟. And let perpetual light * shine upon them.

segments.t: Et lux perpétua * lúceat eis.

content.latin: Psalmus 85 [3]
content.english: Psalm 85 [3]

segments.t: Psalmus 85

content.latin: 85:1 Inclína, Dómine, aurem tuam, et exáudi me: * quóniam inops, et pauper sum ego.
content.english: 85:1 Incline thy ear, O Lord, and hear me: * for I am needy and poor.

segments.t: Inclína, Dómine, aurem tuam, et exáudi me: * quóniam inops, et pauper sum ego.

content.latin: 85:2 Custódi ánimam meam, quóniam sanctus sum: * salvum fac servum tuum, Deus meus, sperántem in te.
content.english: 85:2 Preserve my soul, for I am holy: * save thy servant, O my God, that trusteth in thee.

segments.t: Custódi ánimam meam, quóniam sanctus sum: * salvum fac servum tuum, Deus meus, sperántem in te.

content.latin: 85:3 Miserére mei, Dómine, quóniam ad te clamávi tota die: * lætífica ánimam servi tui, quóniam ad te, Dómine, ánimam meam levávi.
content.english: 85:3 Have mercy on me, O Lord, for I have cried to thee all the day. * Give joy to the soul of thy servant, for to thee, O Lord, I have lifted up my soul.

segments.t: Miserére mei, Dómine, quóniam ad te clamávi tota die: * lætífica ánimam servi tui, quóniam ad te, Dómine, ánimam meam levávi.

content.latin: 85:5 Quóniam tu, Dómine, suávis, et mitis: * et multæ misericórdiæ ómnibus invocántibus te.
content.english: 85:5 For thou, O Lord, art sweet and mild: * and plenteous in mercy to all that call upon thee.

segments.t: Quóniam tu, Dómine, suávis, et mitis: * et multæ misericórdiæ ómnibus invocántibus te.

content.latin: 85:6 Áuribus pércipe, Dómine, oratiónem meam: * et inténde voci deprecatiónis meæ.
content.english: 85:6 Give ear, O Lord, to my prayer: * and attend to the voice of my petition.

segments.t: Áuribus pércipe, Dómine, oratiónem meam: * et inténde voci deprecatiónis meæ.

content.latin: 85:7 In die tribulatiónis meæ clamávi ad te: * quia exaudísti me.
content.english: 85:7 I have called upon thee in the day of my trouble: * because thou hast heard me.

segments.t: In die tribulatiónis meæ clamávi ad te: * quia exaudísti me.

content.latin: 85:8 Non est símilis tui in diis, Dómine: * et non est secúndum ópera tua.
content.english: 85:8 There is none among the gods like unto thee, O Lord: * and there is none according to thy works.

segments.t: Non est símilis tui in diis, Dómine: * et non est secúndum ópera tua.

content.latin: 85:9 Omnes gentes quascúmque fecísti, vénient, et adorábunt coram te, Dómine: * et glorificábunt nomen tuum.
content.english: 85:9 All the nations thou hast made shall come and adore before thee, O Lord: * and they shall glorify thy name.

segments.t: Omnes gentes quascúmque fecísti, vénient, et adorábunt coram te, Dómine: * et glorificábunt nomen tuum.

content.latin: 85:10 Quóniam magnus es tu, et fáciens mirabília: * tu es Deus solus.
content.english: 85:10 For thou art great and dost wonderful things: * thou art God alone.

segments.t: Quóniam magnus es tu, et fáciens mirabília: * tu es Deus solus.

content.latin: 85:11 Deduc me, Dómine, in via tua, et ingrédiar in veritáte tua: * lætétur cor meum ut tímeat nomen tuum.
content.english: 85:11 Conduct me, O Lord, in thy way, and I will walk in thy truth: * let my heart rejoice that it may fear thy name.

segments.t: Deduc me, Dómine, in via tua, et ingrédiar in veritáte tua: * lætétur cor meum ut tímeat nomen tuum.

content.latin: 85:12 Confitébor tibi, Dómine, Deus meus, in toto corde meo, * et glorificábo nomen tuum in ætérnum:
content.english: 85:12 I will praise thee, O Lord my God, with my whole heart, * and I will glorify thy name for ever:

segments.t: Confitébor tibi, Dómine, Deus meus, in toto corde meo, * et glorificábo nomen tuum in ætérnum:

content.latin: 85:13 Quia misericórdia tua magna est super me: * et eruísti ánimam meam ex inférno inferióri.
content.english: 85:13 For thy mercy is great towards me: * and thou hast delivered my soul out of the lower hell.

segments.t: Quia misericórdia tua magna est super me: * et eruísti ánimam meam ex inférno inferióri.

content.latin: 85:14 Deus, iníqui insurrexérunt super me, et synagóga poténtium quæsiérunt ánimam meam: * et non proposuérunt te in conspéctu suo.
content.english: 85:14 O God, the wicked are risen up against me, and the assembly of the mighty have sought my soul: * and they have not set thee before their eyes.

segments.t: Deus, iníqui insurrexérunt super me, et synagóga poténtium quæsiérunt ánimam meam: * et non proposuérunt te in conspéctu suo.

content.latin: 85:15 Et tu, Dómine, Deus miserátor et miséricors, * pátiens, et multæ misericórdiæ, et verax,
content.english: 85:15 And thou, O Lord, art a God of compassion, and merciful, * patient, and of much mercy, and true.

segments.t: Et tu, Dómine, Deus miserátor et miséricors, * pátiens, et multæ misericórdiæ, et verax,

content.latin: 85:16 Réspice in me, et miserére mei, * da impérium tuum púero tuo: et salvum fac fílium ancíllæ tuæ.
content.english: 85:16 O look upon me, and have mercy on me: * give thy command to thy servant, and save the son of thy handmaid.

segments.t: Réspice in me, et miserére mei, * da impérium tuum púero tuo: et salvum fac fílium ancíllæ tuæ.

content.latin: 85:17 Fac mecum signum in bonum, ut vídeant qui odérunt me, et confundántur: * quóniam tu, Dómine, adiuvísti me, et consolátus es me.
content.english: 85:17 Shew me a token for good: that they who hate me may see, and be confounded, * because thou, O Lord, hast helped me and hast comforted me.

segments.t: Fac mecum signum in bonum, ut vídeant qui odérunt me, et confundántur: * quóniam tu, Dómine, adiuvísti me, et consolátus es me.

content.english: ℣. Eternal rest * grant unto them, O Lord.

segments.t: Réquiem ætérnam * dona eis, Dómine.

content.english: ℟. And let perpetual light * shine upon them.

content.latin: Pater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum: advéniat regnum tuum: fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum cotidiánum da nobis hódie: et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris:
content.english: Our Father, who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us.

content.latin: ℣. Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
content.english: ℣. And lead us not into temptation:

segments.t: Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:

content.latin: ℟. Sed líbera nos a malo.
content.english: ℟. But deliver us from evil.

segments.t: Sed líbera nos a malo.

content.latin: ℣. A porta ínferi.
content.english: ℣. From the gates of hell.

segments.t: A porta ínferi.

content.latin: ℟. Erue, Dómine, ánimas eórum.
content.english: ℟. Deliver their souls, O Lord!

segments.t: Erue, Dómine, ánimas eórum.

content.latin: ℣. Requiéscant in pace.
content.english: ℣. May they rest in peace.

segments.t: Requiéscant in pace.

content.english: ℟. Amen.

content.english: ℣. O Lord, hear my prayer.

segments.t: Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.

content.english: ℟. And let my cry come unto thee.

content.english: skip second O Lord, hear my prayer

content.english: Let us pray.

content.latin: Fidélium, Deus, ómnium Cónditor et Redémptor, animábus famulórum famularúmque tuárum remissiónem cunctórum tríbue peccatórum: ut indulgéntiam, quam semper optavérunt, piis supplicatiónibus consequántur:
content.english: O God, who art thyself at once the Maker and the Redeemer of all thy faithful ones, grant unto the souls of thy servants and handmaids remission of all their sins, making of our entreaties unto our great Father a mean whereby they may have that forgiveness which they have ever hoped for.

content.latin: Qui vivis et regnas cum Deo Patre, in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: Who livest and reignest with God the Father in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, world without end.

Psalmus 101(1-13)

content.latin: 101:2 Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam: * et clamor meus ad te véniat.
content.english: 101:2 Hear, O Lord, my prayer: * and let my cry come to thee.

segments.t: Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam: * et clamor meus ad te véniat.

content.latin: 101:3 Non avértas fáciem tuam a me: * in quacúmque die tríbulor, inclína ad me aurem tuam.
content.english: 101:3 Turn not away thy face from me: * in the day when I am in trouble, incline thy ear to me.

segments.t: Non avértas fáciem tuam a me: * in quacúmque die tríbulor, inclína ad me aurem tuam.

content.latin: 101:3 In quacúmque die invocávero te, * velóciter exáudi me.
content.english: 101:3 In what day soever I shall call upon thee, * hear me speedily.

segments.t: In quacúmque die invocávero te, * velóciter exáudi me.

content.latin: 101:4 Quia defecérunt sicut fumus dies mei: * et ossa mea sicut crémium aruérunt.
content.english: 101:4 For my days are vanished like smoke: * and my bones are grown dry like fuel for the fire.

segments.t: Quia defecérunt sicut fumus dies mei: * et ossa mea sicut crémium aruérunt.

content.latin: 101:5 Percússus sum ut fænum, et áruit cor meum: * quia oblítus sum comédere panem meum.
content.english: 101:5 I am smitten as grass, and my heart is withered: * because I forgot to eat my bread.

segments.t: Percússus sum ut fænum, et áruit cor meum: * quia oblítus sum comédere panem meum.

content.latin: 101:6 A voce gémitus mei * adhǽsit os meum carni meæ.
content.english: 101:6 Through the voice of my groaning, * my bone hath cleaved to my flesh.

segments.t: A voce gémitus mei * adhǽsit os meum carni meæ.

content.latin: 101:7 Símilis factus sum pellicáno solitúdinis: * factus sum sicut nyctícorax in domicílio.
content.english: 101:7 I am become like to a pelican of the wilderness: * I am like a night raven in the house.

segments.t: Símilis factus sum pellicáno solitúdinis: * factus sum sicut nyctícorax in domicílio.

content.latin: 101:8 Vigilávi, * et factus sum sicut passer solitárius in tecto.
content.english: 101:8 I have watched, * and am become as a sparrow all alone on the housetop.

segments.t: Vigilávi, * et factus sum sicut passer solitárius in tecto.

content.latin: 101:9 Tota die exprobrábant mihi inimíci mei: * et qui laudábant me, advérsum me iurábant.
content.english: 101:9 All the day long my enemies reproached me: * and they that praised me did swear against me.

segments.t: Tota die exprobrábant mihi inimíci mei: * et qui laudábant me, advérsum me iurábant.

content.latin: 101:10 Quia cínerem tamquam panem manducábam, * et potum meum cum fletu miscébam.
content.english: 101:10 For I did eat ashes like bread, * and mingled my drink with weeping.

segments.t: Quia cínerem tamquam panem manducábam, * et potum meum cum fletu miscébam.

content.latin: 101:11 A fácie iræ et indignatiónis tuæ: * quia élevans allisísti me.
content.english: 101:11 Because of thy anger and indignation: * for having lifted me up thou hast thrown me down.

segments.t: A fácie iræ et indignatiónis tuæ: * quia élevans allisísti me.

content.latin: 101:12 Dies mei sicut umbra declinavérunt: * et ego sicut fænum árui.
content.english: 101:12 My days have declined like a shadow, * and I am withered like grass.

segments.t: Dies mei sicut umbra declinavérunt: * et ego sicut fænum árui.

content.latin: 101:13 Tu autem, Dómine, in ætérnum pérmanes: * et memoriále tuum in generatiónem et generatiónem.
content.english: 101:13 But thou, O Lord, endurest for ever: * and thy memorial to all generations.

segments.t: Tu autem, Dómine, in ætérnum pérmanes: * et memoriále tuum in generatiónem et generatiónem.

content.latin: ℣. Réquiem ætérnam * dona eis, Dómine.
content.english: ℣. Eternal rest * grant unto them, O Lord.

segments.t: Réquiem ætérnam * dona eis, Dómine.

content.latin: ℟. Et lux perpétua * lúceat eis.
content.english: ℟. And let perpetual light * shine upon them.

segments.t: Et lux perpétua * lúceat eis.
Psalmus 101(14-23)

content.latin: 101:14 Tu exsúrgens miseréberis Sion: * quia tempus miseréndi eius, quia venit tempus.
content.english: 101:14 Thou shalt arise and have mercy on Sion: * for it is time to have mercy on it, for the time is come.

segments.t: Tu exsúrgens miseréberis Sion: * quia tempus miseréndi eius, quia venit tempus.

content.latin: 101:15 Quóniam placuérunt servis tuis lápides eius: * et terræ eius miserebúntur.
content.english: 101:15 For the stones thereof have pleased thy servants: * and they shall have pity on the earth thereof.

segments.t: Quóniam placuérunt servis tuis lápides eius: * et terræ eius miserebúntur.

content.latin: 101:16 Et timébunt gentes nomen tuum, Dómine, * et omnes reges terræ glóriam tuam.
content.english: 101:16 And the Gentiles shall fear thy name, O Lord, * and all the kings of the earth thy glory.

segments.t: Et timébunt gentes nomen tuum, Dómine, * et omnes reges terræ glóriam tuam.

content.latin: 101:17 Quia ædificávit Dóminus Sion: * et vidébitur in glória sua.
content.english: 101:17 For the Lord hath built up Sion: * and he shall be seen in his glory.

segments.t: Quia ædificávit Dóminus Sion: * et vidébitur in glória sua.

content.latin: 101:18 Respéxit in oratiónem humílium: * et non sprevit precem eórum.
content.english: 101:18 He hath had regard to the prayer of the humble: * and he hath not despised their petition.

segments.t: Respéxit in oratiónem humílium: * et non sprevit precem eórum.

content.latin: 101:19 Scribántur hæc in generatióne áltera: * et pópulus, qui creábitur, laudábit Dóminum:
content.english: 101:19 Let these things be written unto another generation: * and the people that shall be created shall praise the Lord:

segments.t: Scribántur hæc in generatióne áltera: * et pópulus, qui creábitur, laudábit Dóminum:

content.latin: 101:20 Quia prospéxit de excélso sancto suo: * Dóminus de cælo in terram aspéxit:
content.english: 101:20 Because he hath looked forth from his high sanctuary: * from heaven the Lord hath looked upon the earth.

segments.t: Quia prospéxit de excélso sancto suo: * Dóminus de cælo in terram aspéxit:

content.latin: 101:21 Ut audíret gémitus compeditórum: * ut sólveret fílios interemptórum:
content.english: 101:21 That he might hear the groans of them that are in fetters: * that he might release the children of the slain:

segments.t: Ut audíret gémitus compeditórum: * ut sólveret fílios interemptórum:

content.latin: 101:22 Ut annúntient in Sion nomen Dómini: * et laudem eius in Ierúsalem.
content.english: 101:22 That they may declare the name of the Lord in Sion: * and his praise in Jerusalem;

segments.t: Ut annúntient in Sion nomen Dómini: * et laudem eius in Ierúsalem.

content.latin: 101:23 In conveniéndo pópulos in unum, * et reges ut sérviant Dómino.
content.english: 101:23 When the people assemble together, * and kings, to serve the Lord.

segments.t: In conveniéndo pópulos in unum, * et reges ut sérviant Dómino.

content.latin: ℣. Réquiem ætérnam * dona eis, Dómine.
content.english: ℣. Eternal rest * grant unto them, O Lord.

segments.t: Réquiem ætérnam * dona eis, Dómine.

content.latin: ℟. Et lux perpétua * lúceat eis.
content.english: ℟. And let perpetual light * shine upon them.

segments.t: Et lux perpétua * lúceat eis.
Psalmus 101(24-29)

content.latin: 101:24 Respóndit ei in via virtútis suæ: * Paucitátem diérum meórum núntia mihi.
content.english: 101:24 He answered him in the way of his strength: * Declare unto me the fewness of my days.

segments.t: Respóndit ei in via virtútis suæ: * Paucitátem diérum meórum núntia mihi.

content.latin: 101:25 Ne révoces me in dimídio diérum meórum: * in generatiónem et generatiónem anni tui.
content.english: 101:25 Call me not away in the midst of my days: * thy years are unto generation and generation.

segments.t: Ne révoces me in dimídio diérum meórum: * in generatiónem et generatiónem anni tui.

content.latin: 101:26 Inítio tu, Dómine, terram fundásti: * et ópera mánuum tuárum sunt cæli.
content.english: 101:26 In the beginning, O Lord, thou foundedst the earth: * and the heavens are the works of thy hands.

segments.t: Inítio tu, Dómine, terram fundásti: * et ópera mánuum tuárum sunt cæli.

content.latin: 101:27 Ipsi períbunt, tu autem pérmanes: * et omnes sicut vestiméntum veteráscent.
content.english: 101:27 They shall perish but thou remainest: * and all of them shall grow old like a garment:

segments.t: Ipsi períbunt, tu autem pérmanes: * et omnes sicut vestiméntum veteráscent.

content.latin: 101:28 Et sicut opertórium mutábis eos, et mutabúntur: * tu autem idem ipse es, et anni tui non defícient.
content.english: 101:28 And as a vesture thou shalt change them, and they shall be changed. * But thou art always the selfsame, and thy years shall not fail.

segments.t: Et sicut opertórium mutábis eos, et mutabúntur: * tu autem idem ipse es, et anni tui non defícient.

content.latin: 101:29 Fílii servórum tuórum habitábunt: * et semen eórum in sǽculum dirigétur.
content.english: 101:29 The children of thy servants shall continue: * and their seed shall be directed for ever.

segments.t: Fílii servórum tuórum habitábunt: * et semen eórum in sǽculum dirigétur.

content.latin: ℣. Réquiem ætérnam * dona eis, Dómine.
content.english: ℣. Eternal rest * grant unto them, O Lord.

segments.t: Réquiem ætérnam * dona eis, Dómine.

content.latin: ℟. Et lux perpétua * lúceat eis.
content.english: ℟. And let perpetual light * shine upon them.
